# RioCharts

> Charts for .NET: line, area, bar, scatter, bubble, pie, donut, radial bar, gauge, bullet, funnel, radar, heatmap, calendar heatmap, box plot, histogram, dumbbell, range bar (timeline), candlestick, waterfall, treemap and world map, interactive in Blazor, as PNG and SVG on the server, and from AI agents. This guide covers the Blazor component, the usual way into an app. The chart is laid out in .NET and rendered as SVG; a small JS module only measures text and handles the pointer. Packages are previews (APIs change before 1.0) and target .NET 10 (LTS) and .NET 11.

This is the complete guide for coding agents: setup, rules, examples that compile, and every component parameter. Docs with live examples: https://riocharts.com/

## Setup

1. Add the package (a preview, so `--prerelease` is needed):

   ```shell
   dotnet add package RioCharts.Blazor --prerelease
   ```

2. Add two usings to `_Imports.razor`:

   ```razor
   @using RioCharts.Blazor
   @using RioCharts.Core
   ```

3. That is all. There are no services to register and no script or stylesheet tags: the styles come with the app's `{AssemblyName}.styles.css` bundle (already linked by the Blazor templates) and the JS module loads itself.

Tooltips, zoom, clicks, selection, keyboard navigation and downloads need an interactive page (`@rendermode InteractiveServer`, `InteractiveWebAssembly` or `InteractiveAuto`, or a global interactive render mode). On a static page the chart renders as plain SVG without interaction.

.NET MAUI Blazor Hybrid apps (`dotnet new maui-blazor`) use the same package and usings, nothing else: the chart runs in the app's WebView and is always interactive, so no render mode is needed. Tested on Windows; Android and iOS not yet.

Other packages, only when needed: `RioCharts.Skia` (PNG/SVG export on the server, `ChartExport`), `RioCharts.AI` (chart tools for AI agents), `RioCharts.Core` (the engine alone; RioCharts.Blazor already brings it).

## How it works

- `<RioChart>` holds series as child components (`<LineSeries>`, `<BarSeries>`, ...) and annotations (`<ReferenceLine>`, ...). Series render nothing themselves; the chart lays them out together.
- `Items` goes on the chart (shared by all series) or on each series. `TItem` is inferred from `Items`; set `TItem` on `<RioChart>` when only the series have `Items` or when the chart has event handlers (`OnPointClick`, ...).
- `XValue` returns the x value: `DateTime`/`DateTimeOffset` give a time axis, numbers a linear axis, strings a category axis (categories keep the order of the items).
- `YValue` returns `double?`; `null` leaves a gap. Cast `decimal` to `double`.
- Data over several powers of ten (1 to 1,000,000): a log y axis, `YAxis="@(new AxisOptions { Scale = ScaleType.Log })"` (`"scale": "log"` in JSON definitions). Values of zero or below are left out. The same on `XAxis` for numeric x under lines and scatter points (not bars), e.g. load time against page size, log on both axes.
- Many categories (e.g. bars per country): labels that do not fit slope at 45 degrees, so all show. `XAxis="@(new AxisOptions { LabelRotation = 90 })"` sets another angle; `LabelRotation = 0` keeps them horizontal and shows every n-th.
- Largest first: `Sort="SortOrder.Descending"` on a `BarSeries` orders the categories by its values after `Aggregate` (e.g. counts). Sorting `Items` does not help with aggregates.
- One y axis per unit: `YAxes="@([new AxisOptions { Id = "kw", Title = "kW" }])"` on the chart and `YAxisId="kw"` on the series. Extra axes go right unless `Position = AxisPosition.Left`; several on one side sit side by side. Add `SeriesColor = true` to each axis to color it like its series.
- Few points on a line (say under 20): `Highlight="PointHighlight.All"` puts a dot on every point (`MarkerSize` for the diameter). Other values mark single points: `First`, `Last`, `Min`, `Max`, combined with `|`.
- Bars never take more than a fifth of the plot, so a lone bar after filtering stays narrow; `MaxBarWidth="40"` on a `BarSeries` caps them in pixels.
- Pins: `OnPointClick` gives the item; add a `<PointAnnotation Id="..." X="item.Time" Y="item.Value" />` for it. With `OnAnnotationClick` set, a click on the pin raises `OnAnnotationClick` (with its `Id`), even on a data point: remove the pin there.
- Tooltip time: `XAxis="@(new AxisOptions { TooltipFormat = "d MMM HH:mm" })"` formats the tooltip header only (no seconds, no zone offset); `Format` is for the axis labels.
- Several items with the same x: `Aggregate="Aggregate.Sum"` (also Average, Min, Max, Count, Last), or `YAggregate="g => ..."` with your own calculation over the group.
- Error bars (bar, line and scatter series): `ErrorValue="m => m.StdDev"` (plus or minus, per item), `Error="2.5"` (the same for every point), or `ErrorLowValue` and `ErrorHighValue` (the ends, as values). JSON: `errorField`, `error`, `errorLow` and `errorHigh`.
- Time x per hour, day, month...: `Bucket="TimeBucket.Day"` on line, area and bar series gives one point per bucket, combined with `Aggregate` (average when not set). `TimeBucket.Auto` picks the bucket from the data's time span (about 50 points). With `TimeZone` on the chart, buckets follow that zone's calendar (a day is midnight to midnight there). No need to group in the query.
- Updates: selectors run once per data change. The chart reprocesses a series when `Items` is a new reference or `DataVersion` changes. Changing a list in place does nothing until you assign a new list or change `DataVersion`. For streaming data use a `SeriesBuffer`.
- Size: the chart fills its container's width; `Height` is 300 px by default.
- Number formats are .NET format strings (`Format="#,0 €"`, `"0.0 °C"`, `"0'%'"`) in the chart's `Culture` (default: the current culture).
- Colors: CSS colors or theme variables, e.g. `Color="#2563eb"` or `Color="--rio-negative"`. The palette and light/dark theme come from CSS variables (`--rio-series-1` ... `--rio-series-10`, `--rio-text`, ...).
- Namespaces beyond the two usings: `RioCharts.Core.Data` (`SeriesData`, `SeriesBuffer`), `RioCharts.Core.Definitions` (`ChartDataset`, `ChartDefinitionJson`).

## Choosing a series

| To show | Component | Key parameters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Change over time, trends | `LineSeries` | `XValue`, `YValue`, `Curve` |
| Volume over time, parts of a total over time | `AreaSeries` | `Stack` to stack |
| Compare categories | `BarSeries` | `Aggregate`, `Stack`, `Horizontal="true"` on the chart |
| Shares per x value (100 % stacked) | `BarSeries`, `AreaSeries` | `YAxis="@(new AxisOptions { Stacking = StackMode.Percent })"` on the chart |
| Min to max band | `RangeAreaSeries` | `LowValue`, `YValue` |
| Relation between two numbers | `ScatterSeries` | `XValue` and `YValue` numeric, `TrendLine` |
| Three numbers per item (x, y and a size) | `ScatterSeries` with `SizeValue` | bubbles; `SizeName` labels the size in the tooltip |
| Shares of a whole | `PieSeries`, `DonutSeries` | `GroupSmallSlices` |
| Progress toward a goal | `RadialBarSeries` | `Max` |
| One value on a scale (load, how full), with ranges and a target | `GaugeSeries` | `Value` (or `YValue` per item, `XValue` its label), `Max`, `Target`, `ColorBands` |
| Values against targets in little space (KPIs) | `BulletSeries` | one per measure with `Value`, `Max`, `Target`; or Items with `XValue`, `YValue`, `TargetValue` |
| Stages narrowing down (visits → cart → purchase) | `FunnelSeries` | `XValue` (the stage), `YValue`; stages keep the items' order, each shows its share of the stage before; one funnel per chart |
| Several measures per item | `RadarSeries` | one series per item |
| A value per day over months or a year (orders, activity) | `CalendarSeries` | `XValue` a date or time; items on the same day add up (`Aggregate` to change), no `YValue` counts them; one calendar per chart |
| Values over two categories (hour × day) | `HeatmapSeries` | one series per row (`Name`); `XValue` the column, `YValue` the color; `Midpoint="0"` for changes (two colors) |
| Spread of values | `BoxPlotSeries` | raw values, or `Q1Value`, `MedianValue`, `Q3Value`; `Horizontal="true"` on the chart for rows |
| Distribution of values (e.g. response times) | `HistogramSeries` | one item per value, `XValue` the value; `BinWidth` or `BinCount` |
| Two values per category (before/after, plan/actual) | `DumbbellSeries` | `XValue` the category, `FromValue` the first value, `YValue` the second; `Horizontal="true"` on the chart for rows |
| Periods per row on a time axis (schedule, states over time) | `RangeBarSeries` | `RowValue`, `StartValue`, `EndValue`; one series per state |
| Open, high, low, close | `CandlestickSeries` | `OpenValue`, `HighValue`, `LowValue`, `CloseValue`, or raw values with `Bucket` |
| From a start value to an end value (result, budget) | `WaterfallSeries` | `YValue` the change, `IsTotal` marks totals; `Horizontal="true"` on the chart for rows |
| Hierarchy by size | `TreemapSeries` | `XValue` (path or name), `ParentValue`, `VisibleLevels` |
| Values per country, places on a world map | `MapSeries`, `MapBubbleSeries` | `MapSeries`: `XValue` the country code ("SE") or English name, `YValue` the value; `MapBubbleSeries`: `XValue` the place's name, `YValue` its size, `Latitude`, `Longitude`; `Projection="MapProjection.Mercator"` on the chart for the web-map look |

Check the parameters of each component in the reference below before using them.

## Examples

Each example is a complete component file. These exact files are compiled and rendered by the RioCharts tests.

### Line chart over time

Two series from one list of items. Times give a time axis; more than one series adds a legend.

```razor
<RioChart Items="visits" Title="Visits per day" YAxis="@(new AxisOptions { Title = "Visits" })">
    <LineSeries Name="Web" XValue="v => v.Day" YValue="v => v.Web" Format="#,0" />
    <LineSeries Name="App" XValue="v => v.Day" YValue="v => v.App" Format="#,0" Curve="CurveType.Monotone" />
</RioChart>

@code {
    private sealed record DayVisits(DateTime Day, double Web, double App);

    private readonly List<DayVisits> visits =
    [
        new(new DateTime(2026, 3, 2), 1240, 860),
        new(new DateTime(2026, 3, 3), 1310, 905),
        new(new DateTime(2026, 3, 4), 1185, 940),
        new(new DateTime(2026, 3, 5), 1420, 990),
        new(new DateTime(2026, 3, 6), 1530, 1080),
    ];
}
```

### Bars summed per category

Raw items in, one bar per category: Aggregate sums the items with the same x. Categories keep the order of the items.

```razor
<RioChart Items="orders" Title="Order value per country">
    <BarSeries Name="Value" XValue="o => o.Country" YValue="o => (double)o.Value" Aggregate="Aggregate.Sum"
               Format="#,0 €" DataLabels="true" />
</RioChart>

@code {
    private sealed record Order(string Country, decimal Value);

    private readonly List<Order> orders =
    [
        new("Sweden", 120), new("Norway", 80), new("Sweden", 95),
        new("Denmark", 60), new("Norway", 45), new("Finland", 70),
    ];
}
```

### Stacked bars

Series with the same Stack value stack on each other.

```razor
<RioChart Items="sales" Title="Sales per month, k€">
    <BarSeries Name="Shoes" XValue="s => s.Month" YValue="s => s.Shoes" Stack="total" />
    <BarSeries Name="Clothing" XValue="s => s.Month" YValue="s => s.Clothing" Stack="total" />
    <BarSeries Name="Gear" XValue="s => s.Month" YValue="s => s.Gear" Stack="total" />
</RioChart>

@code {
    private sealed record MonthSales(string Month, double Shoes, double Clothing, double Gear);

    private readonly List<MonthSales> sales =
    [
        new("Jan", 42, 61, 18),
        new("Feb", 38, 57, 22),
        new("Mar", 51, 66, 25),
    ];
}
```

### Donut (or pie)

Shares of a whole. GroupSmallSlices puts slices under 3 % into "Other". PieSeries takes the same parameters.

```razor
<RioChart Items="channels" Title="Revenue by channel">
    <DonutSeries XValue="c => c.Name" YValue="c => c.Revenue" Format="0 k€" GroupSmallSlices="0.03" />
</RioChart>

@code {
    private sealed record Channel(string Name, double Revenue);

    private readonly List<Channel> channels =
    [
        new("Web shop", 420), new("Stores", 310), new("Marketplaces", 150), new("Phone", 12),
    ];
}
```

### Two y axes and a target line

Extra axes in YAxes go on the right; a series picks one with YAxisId. Annotations are child components.

```razor
<RioChart Items="days" YAxis="@(new AxisOptions { Title = "Orders" })"
          YAxes="@([new AxisOptions { Id = "rate", Title = "Conversion, %" }])">
    <BarSeries Name="Orders" XValue="d => d.Day" YValue="d => d.Orders" />
    <LineSeries Name="Conversion" XValue="d => d.Day" YValue="d => d.Conversion" YAxisId="rate" Format="0.0'%'" />
    <ReferenceLine Value="300" Label="Target" />
</RioChart>

@code {
    private sealed record DayStats(string Day, double Orders, double Conversion);

    private readonly List<DayStats> days =
    [
        new("Mon", 280, 2.1), new("Tue", 310, 2.4), new("Wed", 265, 1.9), new("Thu", 340, 2.6), new("Fri", 390, 2.9),
    ];
}
```

### Clicks, zoom and downloads

Needs an interactive page (@rendermode InteractiveServer, InteractiveWebAssembly or InteractiveAuto); static pages show the chart without interaction.

```razor
<RioChart TItem="Reading" Items="readings" Zoomable="true" Exportable="true" OnPointClick="e => clicked = e">
    <LineSeries Name="Temperature" XValue="r => r.Time" YValue="r => r.Celsius" Format="0.0 °C" />
</RioChart>

@if (clicked is not null)
{
    <p>@clicked.SeriesName at @clicked.X: @clicked.Y °C</p>
}

@code {
    private sealed record Reading(DateTime Time, double? Celsius); // null leaves a gap in the line

    private PointClickEventArgs<Reading>? clicked;

    private readonly List<Reading> readings =
        [.. Enumerable.Range(0, 48).Select(h => new Reading(new DateTime(2026, 6, 1).AddHours(h), 18 + 6 * Math.Sin(h / 24.0 * 2 * Math.PI)))];
}
```

### Live data

Append to a SeriesBuffer from any thread; the chart redraws at most every RefreshInterval ms. With a buffer, TItem is not used: set it to double.

```razor
@using RioCharts.Core.Data
@implements IDisposable

<RioChart TItem="double" RefreshInterval="250">
    <LineSeries Name="Requests per second" Buffer="requests" Curve="CurveType.Monotone" />
</RioChart>

@code {
    private readonly SeriesBuffer requests = new(timeWindow: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(2));
    private Timer? timer;

    protected override void OnInitialized() =>
        timer = new Timer(_ => requests.Append(DateTime.Now, Random.Shared.Next(80, 120)), null, 0, 500);

    public void Dispose() => timer?.Dispose();
}
```

### A chart built in code

A ChartDefinition (the same model as a chart definition in JSON) with datasets instead of child components, e.g. for charts chosen at runtime. Fields are camelCase property names.

```razor
@using RioCharts.Core.Definitions

<RioChart TItem="object" Definition="chart" Datasets="datasets" Height="280" />

@code {
    private sealed record Sale(string Region, double Amount);

    private readonly ChartDefinition chart = new()
    {
        Title = "Sales per region",
        Series = [new SeriesOptions { Id = "sales", Type = SeriesType.Bar, Dataset = "sales", X = "region", Y = "amount", Aggregate = Aggregate.Sum }],
    };

    private readonly Dictionary<string, ChartDataset> datasets = new()
    {
        ["sales"] = ChartDataset.FromItems("sales", new[] { new Sale("North", 120), new Sale("South", 95), new Sale("North", 40) }),
    };
}
```

## Common mistakes

- No interactive render mode: the chart shows, but tooltips, zoom, clicks and downloads do nothing. Add `@rendermode InteractiveServer` (or WebAssembly/Auto) to the page.
- Changing a `List<T>` in place (`Add`, `Remove`) and expecting the chart to update: assign a new list, or change `DataVersion`.
- `YValue="x => x.Amount"` where `Amount` is `decimal`: write `(double)x.Amount`.
- Several series with their own `Items` and no `TItem` on `<RioChart>`: set `TItem="YourType"`.
- An event handler lambda (`OnPointClick="e => clicked = e"`) without `TItem`: Blazor cannot infer `TItem` through it and reports errors such as "Cannot convert lambda expression". Set `TItem="YourType"` on `<RioChart>`.
- Blazor-ApexCharts names: there is no `ApexPointSeries` or `SeriesType` parameter; each type is its own component (`<BarSeries>`, `<LineSeries>`, ...). `XValue`, `YValue`, `YAggregate` work as in ApexCharts.
- Animation options (ApexCharts `Animations`, Chart.js `animation`): there are none. Charts are not animated; the series only fade in on first render. `Animate="false"` turns that off.
- Setting a width: not needed, the chart follows its container. Set `Height` for another height.
- Types not found (`SeriesData`, `SeriesBuffer`, `ChartDataset`): add `@using RioCharts.Core.Data` or `@using RioCharts.Core.Definitions`.
- Hard-coded colors for light and dark: use theme variables such as `--rio-negative` and `--rio-positive`; they follow the theme.

## Reference

Every public component and its parameters, from the XML docs. Types in `RioCharts.Core` and `RioCharts.Blazor` used by parameters follow the components.

### Components

#### `<RioChart>` (`RioChart<TItem>`)

A chart. Series are added as child components: `<RioChart Items="readings"><LineSeries XValue="r => r.Time" YValue="r => r.Sessions" /></RioChart>` The chart fills its container's width and lays out again when the width changes.

- `Items`: `IEnumerable<TItem>?` — Items shared by all series that do not set their own.
- `ChildContent`: `RenderFragment?` — The series and annotation components, e.g. <LineSeries> and <ReferenceLine>.
- `Title`: `string?` — Title shown above the chart.
- `Height`: `double` = `300` — Height in pixels. Default 300.
- `Width`: `double?` — Fixed width in pixels. Default: the container's width (responsive).
- `TreemapPath`: `string?` — Treemaps: the group shown (drill-down), as a path with the series' separator, e.g. `"Asia"` or `"Asia/India"`; null shows the whole tree. Maps: the area zoomed into, a continent (`"Europe"`) or a country (`"SE"`); null shows the world. Two-way bindable with `@bind-TreemapPath`, e.g. to keep it in the page's URL.
- `Exportable`: `bool` — Shows a download button in the chart's top-right corner (on hover or focus) with a menu for SVG, PNG and CSV. The same exports are available from code: `RioChart.DownloadPngAsync` etc.
- `ExportFormats`: `ExportFormats` = `ExportFormats.All` — The formats in the download menu. Default all. With a single format the button saves it directly, without a menu; with none there is no button.
- `ExportFileName`: `string?` — File name without extension for downloads. Default: the title, else "chart".
- `XAxis`: `AxisOptions?` — The horizontal axis: title, range, scale and label format. Default: the scale is picked from the data.
- `YAxis`: `AxisOptions?` — The primary vertical axis (id "y" unless set).
- `YAxes`: `IReadOnlyList<AxisOptions>?` — Additional vertical axes; series pick one with `YAxisId`.
- `Legend`: `LegendOptions?` — Legend settings. Default: at the top, shown when there is more than one series.
- `Tooltip`: `TooltipOptions?` — Tooltip settings. On and shared across series by default.
- `TooltipHeader`: `Func<TooltipPoint<TItem>, string?>?` — Text for the tooltip header from the hovered point, e.g. `p => $"Week {Iso(p.X)}"`; null keeps the default (the formatted x, or the series name for nested pies). Runs once per layout for the points that can be hovered, not on pointer moves.
- `TooltipTemplate`: `RenderFragment<TooltipContext<TItem>>?` — Custom tooltip content (Razor), rendered inside the tooltip card. The crosshair still follows the pointer in the browser; the content is rendered by .NET when the hovered x changes, so on Blazor Server it follows one network round trip behind. Prefer `RioChart.TooltipHeader` and the series' `TooltipValue` when text is enough.
- `Annotations`: `IReadOnlyList<Annotation>?` — Annotations as data (in addition to <ReferenceLine> and <ReferenceBand> children).
- `TimeZone`: `string?` — Display time zone: "UTC", "local" (the viewer's browser zone) or an IANA id such as "Europe/Stockholm". Default: none, times are shown as given. With a zone, times are plotted on instants (no doubling back at DST changes) and labelled in that zone.
- `UnspecifiedTimes`: `UnspecifiedTimes?` — With a TimeZone: how DateTime values with Kind Unspecified are read (UTC or the display zone).
- `Culture`: `CultureInfo?` — Culture for labels. Default: the current culture.
- `Texts`: `ChartTexts?` — The chart's own texts ("Reset zoom", "No data available", the download menu, screen reader texts), e.g. `ChartTexts.Swedish with { ResetZoom = "Visa allt" }`. Default: a `ChartTexts` cascaded by the app, else `ChartTexts.For` the `RioChart.Culture` or, without one, the current UI culture.
- `HiddenSeries`: `IReadOnlyCollection<string>?` — Ids of hidden series. Two-way bindable with `@bind-HiddenSeries`.
- `Zoomable`: `bool` — Zoom and pan on the x axis: drag to zoom in, Shift+drag to pan, Ctrl/⌘+wheel to zoom at the pointer, pinch or two-finger drag on touch screens, double-click or the reset button to zoom out. Not for category axes.
- `VisibleRange`: `ChartRange?` — The visible x range (null: all data). Two-way bindable with `@bind-VisibleRange`.
- `Group`: `string?` — Charts with the same group name share the crosshair and (when zoomable) the zoom. They should have the same kind of x axis.
- `SeriesLayer`: `SeriesLayer` — Draw the series as SVG (default) or on a canvas: no DOM per series, for large or many series. Axes, labels and annotations stay SVG (annotations then sit under the series).
- `DownsampleThreshold`: `int?` — Line and area series with more points than this are downsampled (LTTB). Default: twice the plot width, four times on a canvas.
- `RefreshInterval`: `int` = `100` — Live data (series with a `Buffer`): the shortest time between redraws, in milliseconds. Default 100.
- `Compact`: `bool` — Compact chart (sparkline): no axes, grid, legend or title; the series fill the box and the y range fits the data (bars keep zero). Set a small `RioChart.Height` too, e.g. 32. Keyboard navigation is off unless `RioChart.KeyboardNavigation` is set; the chart has a short text summary.
- `AutoCompact`: `bool` = `true` — Default true: as the chart gets small (a narrow container, a low `RioChart.Height`), it leaves out axis titles first, then the legend, the title and the axis labels, so the plot keeps the space; the tooltip still shows the series and values. Below 120 × 60 px it becomes a compact chart. False keeps everything at any size.
- `Horizontal`: `bool` — Bar, box plot, waterfall and dumbbell charts: they run left to right, with the categories down the side (first on top). For rankings and long category names. `RioChart.YAxis` (title, format, min, max) applies to the values.
- `Projection`: `MapProjection` — Maps: how the round world is drawn flat. `MapProjection.EqualEarth` (default) keeps every country's true relative size; `MapProjection.Mercator` is the projection of web maps, with familiar shapes but areas that grow toward the poles. Overrides a `RioChart.Definition`'s projection unless left at the default.
- `Interactive`: `bool` = `true` — False draws plain SVG without the JS module: no tooltip, hover, zoom, keyboard navigation, download button or width measuring. For many small charts (compact charts in a table) or static pages. Set `RioChart.Width` for exact geometry; otherwise the chart is laid out at a default width (640, compact 160) and scaled to fit. Read once, when the chart first renders.
- `KeyboardNavigation`: `bool?` — Keyboard navigation (default on, off for compact charts): the chart is a tab stop, and with it focused the arrow keys move between points (Up/Down: between series; pies: between slices), showing the tooltip and announcing the point to screen readers; Enter clicks it, Escape leaves. With `RioChart.Zoomable`, + and - zoom around the focused point, Shift+Left/Right pans and 0 resets. Handled in the browser.
- `Animate`: `bool` = `true` — False turns off all motion: the short fade when the series first appear, and the fades of the tooltip, buttons and dimmed series. Charts never animate data changes, zoom or streaming either way, and motion is always off when the user asks for reduced motion. To change only the fade's length, set the CSS variable `--rio-enter-duration` (default `0.35s`; `0s` turns it off).
- `Class`: `string?` — Extra CSS class on the container.
- `Definition`: `ChartDefinition?` — A chart definition (e.g. from JSON or an AI agent) instead of child components: series read their x and y fields from `RioChart.Datasets` or the definition's inline data. Layout options such as Height, Culture and HiddenSeries still come from the component.
- `Datasets`: `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ChartDataset>?` — Datasets that a `RioChart.Definition` refers to, by name.
- `Selection`: `SelectionMode` — What the user can select: points (click) or an x range (drag). Default none. Selections from code (`RioChart.SelectedItems`, `RioChart.SelectedRange`, `RioChart.SelectItemsAsync`) show either way. Points need items (not columnar data). Drawn on vertical cartesian charts.
- `SelectedItems`: `IReadOnlyCollection<TItem>?` — The selected items. Two-way bindable with `@bind-SelectedItems`.
- `SelectedRange`: `ChartRange?` — The selected x range (null: none). Two-way bindable with `@bind-SelectedRange`.
- `OnLegendClicking`: `EventCallback<LegendClickingEventArgs>` — Raised before a legend click shows or hides a series; set `Cancel` to keep it as it is. `RioChart.OnLegendClick` follows only when the series was toggled.
- `TreemapPathChanged`: `EventCallback<string?>` — Raised when the group shown changes (two-way binding of `RioChart.TreemapPath`).
- `OnDrillDown`: `EventCallback<string?>` — Treemaps: raised when the shown group changes (a click on a group or the path bar, or `RioChart.DrillDownAsync`), with its path (e.g. "Asia/India"); null for the whole tree.
- `OnExporting`: `EventCallback<ChartExportingEventArgs>` — Raised when the user picks a format in the download menu, before the file is saved: rename it, change the options, or cancel the download and handle the content yourself. Not raised for the export methods called from code.
- `HiddenSeriesChanged`: `EventCallback<IReadOnlyCollection<string>>` — Called with the new hidden series when the user toggles one in the legend.
- `OnLegendClick`: `EventCallback<LegendClickEventArgs>` — Raised after a legend click has toggled a series.
- `OnPointClick`: `EventCallback<PointClickEventArgs<TItem>>` — Raised when a point or bar is clicked.
- `OnAnnotationClick`: `EventCallback<AnnotationClickEventArgs>` — Raised when an annotation is clicked: a reference line or band, a point annotation or a callout (each becomes a focusable button). A click on a point annotation's marker, label or callout box is the annotation's, even when it sits on a data point; elsewhere a point or bar under the pointer wins over an annotation underneath.
- `OnAnnotationChanged`: `EventCallback<AnnotationChangedEventArgs>` — Raised when the user has dragged a reference line (`Draggable`). For lines in `RioChart.Annotations`, update the definition's value here; components use `@bind-Value`.
- `VisibleRangeChanged`: `EventCallback<ChartRange?>` — Called with the new visible range after a zoom, pan or reset (null: all data).
- `OnZoomChanging`: `EventCallback<ZoomChangingEventArgs>` — Raised before a zoom or pan is applied; the handler may change or cancel it.
- `SelectedItemsChanged`: `EventCallback<IReadOnlyCollection<TItem>>` — Called with the selected items when the selection changes.
- `SelectedRangeChanged`: `EventCallback<ChartRange?>` — Called with the selected range when the selection changes (null: none).
- `OnSelectionChanged`: `EventCallback<SelectionChangedEventArgs<TItem>>` — Raised when the selection changes, by the user or from code.

##### Methods (call through `@ref`)

- `string? GetTreemapPath()` — Treemaps: the group shown, as a path with the series' separator; null when the whole tree is shown (or the path is not there).
- `Task DrillDownAsync(string? path)` — Treemaps: shows a group (drill-down), e.g. `"Asia"` or `"Asia/India"` (the series' path separator), as clicking it does; null or "" shows the whole tree. A path that is not there shows the whole tree.
- `bool IsSeriesVisible(string seriesId)` — Whether a series is shown (not hidden through the legend, `RioChart.HiddenSeries` or code).
- `Task ShowSeriesAsync(string seriesId)` — Shows a hidden series (raises `HiddenSeriesChanged`).
- `Task HideSeriesAsync(string seriesId)` — Hides a series; it keeps its color and legend item (raises `HiddenSeriesChanged`).
- `Task ToggleSeriesAsync(string seriesId)` — Shows a hidden series or hides a shown one, as a legend click does (without the legend events).
- `Task HighlightSeriesAsync(string? seriesId)` — Fades every series but this one (and their data labels), e.g. while a matching table row is hovered; null shows all again. Hovering or focusing a legend item does the same for its series meanwhile. SVG series layer; needs JS (interactive rendering).
- `string? GetHighlightedSeries()` — The series highlighted with `RioChart.HighlightSeriesAsync`, or null.
- `ChartPoint? ValueToPixel(object x, double y, string? yAxis = null)` — The chart position of a data value, e.g. to place your own element over the chart: x as a DateTime, number or category name, y on the given axis (default: the first). Positions outside the plot are returned too. Null before the first layout, for an x not on the axis, and for pies and horizontal bars.
- `ChartValue? PixelToValue(double x, double y, string? yAxis = null)` — The data value at a chart position (CSS pixels from the chart's top left), e.g. from a mouse event: x as a DateTime, number or the nearest category's name, y on the given axis (default: the first). Null before the first layout, and for pies and horizontal bars.
- `Task ApplyAsync(Func<Task> changes)` — Runs several changes (zoom, selection, hidden series, …) and draws the chart once at the end instead of after each. Events and bound parameters are raised as the changes happen. Matters most on Blazor Server, where each render is a round trip.
- `Task<string> ExportSvgAsync(ChartImageOptions? options = null)` — The chart as a standalone SVG document, as currently drawn (size, zoom, hidden series and theme colors resolved). Needs an interactive render mode.
- `Task<byte[]> ExportPngAsync(ChartImageOptions? options = null)` — The chart as a PNG image, as currently drawn. Needs an interactive render mode.
- `string ExportCsv(CsvOptions? options = null)` — The data of every series (hidden ones too) as CSV: an x column and one column per series. Works without a browser. See `ChartCsv`.
- `Task DownloadSvgAsync(string? fileName = null, ChartImageOptions? options = null)` — Saves the chart as an SVG file in the browser (file name without extension; default `RioChart.ExportFileName`). Does nothing once the browser has disconnected.
- `Task DownloadPngAsync(string? fileName = null, ChartImageOptions? options = null)` — Saves the chart as a PNG file in the browser. Does nothing once the browser has disconnected.
- `Task DownloadCsvAsync(string? fileName = null, CsvOptions? options = null)` — Saves the data as a CSV file in the browser. Does nothing once the browser has disconnected.
- `ChartDefinition GetDefinition()` — The chart model: the `RioChart.Definition` parameter, or one built from the parameters and child components (for saving, or as a starting point for edits).
- `void Refresh()` — Lays out again, e.g. after changing data in place without a new reference or DataVersion.
- `ChartRange? GetVisibleRange()` — The visible x range, or null when all data is shown.
- `Task ZoomToAsync(ChartRange range)` — Shows the given x range (clamped to the data).
- `Task ResetZoomAsync()` — Shows all data again.
- `Task PanAsync(double fraction)` — Moves the visible range by a fraction of its width (negative: left).
- `IReadOnlyList<TItem> GetSelectedItems()` — The selected items: the selected points', or those of the points in the selected range.
- `ChartRange? GetSelectedRange()` — The selected x range, or null.
- `Task SelectItemsAsync(IEnumerable<TItem> items)` — Selects the points of these items (replacing the selection).
- `Task SelectRangeAsync(ChartRange? range)` — Selects an x range (replacing the selection); null clears it.
- `Task ClearSelectionAsync()` — Clears the selection.
- `IReadOnlyList<TItem> GetItemsInRange(ChartRange range)` — The items of the visible series' points inside an x range, in series order, each once. Empty for columnar data and category axes.
- `Task ShowTooltipAsync(object x)` — Shows the crosshair and tooltip at an x value (DateTime, number or category name), as if the pointer were there; linked charts (same `RioChart.Group`) show their crosshair too. It stays until `RioChart.HideTooltipAsync`, also across new data, and comes back after the pointer leaves the chart. Cartesian charts; needs JS (interactive rendering).
- `Task HideTooltipAsync()` — Hides the tooltip shown with `RioChart.ShowTooltipAsync`.

#### Parameters of every series (`SeriesBase<TItem>`)

Every series component below takes these, plus its own.

- `Items`: `IEnumerable<TItem>?` — Items to plot. Defaults to the chart's Items.
- `Id`: `string?` — Unique id (used by `HiddenSeries`). Defaults to `SeriesBase.Name`, else generated.
- `Name`: `string?` — Name shown in the legend.
- `XValue`: `Func<TItem, object?>?` — X value: a number, DateTime, DateTimeOffset, DateOnly or string (category).
- `YValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Y value; null leaves a gap.
- `Aggregate`: `Aggregate?` — Combines items with the same x into one point: the Sum, Average, Min, Max or Last of `SeriesBase.YValue`, or the Count of items (needs no YValue). Use `SeriesBase.YAggregate` for anything else. Without either, items with the same x are drawn on top of each other.
- `YAggregate`: `Func<IReadOnlyList<TItem>, double?>?` — Combines items with the same x into one point, with y computed from the group, e.g. `g => g.Sum(o => o.Amount)`; null leaves a gap. Used instead of `SeriesBase.YValue` and `SeriesBase.Aggregate` when set. A clicked point's items are in `PointClickEventArgs.Items`.
- `Data`: `SeriesData?` — Columnar data (fast path for large series); used instead of Items when set.
- `DataVersion`: `object?` — Change this to reprocess the data after changing Items in place.
- `Color`: `string?` — CSS color. Defaults to the next palette color.
- `ColorValue`: `Func<TItem, string?>?` — A color per item, e.g. `o => o.Late ? "--rio-negative" : null`: a CSS color or a theme token (tokens follow light and dark themes); null keeps the series color. Bars, scatter markers, pie slices, radial bars and treemap items take the color; lines and areas mark the point with a dot in it. Aggregated points take their first item's color. Runs once per data change, like the other selectors.
- `ColorBands`: `IReadOnlyList<ColorBand>?` — Colors by value, e.g. `[new() { Above = 120, Color = "--rio-negative" }]`: a line or area changes color where it crosses into a band, a bar or scatter point takes the color of the band its value is in. Later bands win where they overlap; `SeriesBase.ColorValue` wins over bands.
- `ZIndex`: `int?` — Draw order override (default: areas, then bars, then lines).
- `YAxisId`: `string?` — Id of the vertical axis to use (see `RioChart.YAxes`). Default: the primary axis.
- `Stack`: `string?` — Stack group: series of the same type with the same stack name are stacked.
- `DataLabels`: `bool?` — Show values on the chart. Default: off, except for pie, donut and radial bar.
- `Format`: `string?` — .NET format string for values in tooltips and data labels, e.g. "0.0".
- `TooltipValue`: `Func<TooltipPoint<TItem>, string?>?` — Text for this series' value in the tooltip, e.g. `p => $"{p.Y:0} ms"` or `p => $"{p.Y:0} ms (target {p.Item!.Target} ms)"`; null keeps the default (`SeriesBase.Format`). Runs once per layout for the points that can be hovered, not on pointer moves.
- `Buffer`: `SeriesBuffer?` — Live data (used instead of Items and Data when set). Append to it from any thread; the chart redraws at most every `RioChart.RefreshInterval` milliseconds.

#### `<LineSeries>` (`LineSeries<TItem>`)

Line series.

- `Bucket`: `TimeBucket?` — Time x: one point per bucket (e.g. `TimeBucket.Day` or `TimeBucket.Month`, on the items' wall-clock time, or in the chart's `TimeZone` when set) at the bucket's start, combining its items with `Aggregate` (average when not set) or `YAggregate`. `TimeBucket.Auto` picks the bucket from the data's time span (about 50 buckets).
- `Curve`: `CurveType` — Line shape: Linear, Monotone (smooth, no overshoot) or Step.
- `StrokeWidth`: `double` = `2` — Line width in pixels.
- `Highlight`: `PointHighlight` — Points to mark with a dot, e.g. `PointHighlight.Last | PointHighlight.Max`, or `PointHighlight.All` for a dot on every point (sparse data: shows where the values are; not drawn beyond 1000 visible points). Default none.
- `MarkerSize`: `double?` — Diameter of the `LineSeries.Highlight` dots in pixels. Default: from the line width (for a 2 px line, 5 px; 7 px with `PointHighlight.All`).
- `Sort`: `SortOrder?` — Category x: orders the categories by this series' values (after `Aggregate`, e.g. counts), largest first with `SortOrder.Descending`. The first series with a sort decides for the whole chart. Time and number x ignore it.
- `Error`: `double?` — Error bars: the same plus-or-minus amount for every point, e.g. 2.5.
- `ErrorValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Error bars: each item's plus-or-minus amount, e.g. `m => m.StdDev`; null for none. Items combined into one point take the average.
- `ErrorLowValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Error bars: the low end of each item's error bar (a value, e.g. a confidence interval's lower bound); use with `ErrorBarSeriesBase.ErrorHighValue`. Items combined into one point take the lowest.
- `ErrorHighValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Error bars: the high end of each item's error bar; use with `ErrorBarSeriesBase.ErrorLowValue`. Items combined into one point take the highest.

#### `<AreaSeries>` (`AreaSeries<TItem>`)

Area series, filled down to zero.

- `Bucket`: `TimeBucket?` — Time x: one point per bucket (e.g. `TimeBucket.Day` or `TimeBucket.Month`, on the items' wall-clock time, or in the chart's `TimeZone` when set) at the bucket's start, combining its items with `Aggregate` (average when not set) or `YAggregate`. `TimeBucket.Auto` picks the bucket from the data's time span (about 50 buckets).
- `Curve`: `CurveType` — Shape of the top edge: Linear, Monotone (smooth, no overshoot) or Step.
- `StrokeWidth`: `double` = `2` — Width of the top line in pixels. Default 2.
- `Highlight`: `PointHighlight` — Points to mark with a dot, e.g. `PointHighlight.Last`, or `PointHighlight.All` for every point. Default none.
- `MarkerSize`: `double?` — Diameter of the `AreaSeries.Highlight` dots in pixels. Default: from the line width.
- `Sort`: `SortOrder?` — Category x: orders the categories by this series' values (after `Aggregate`, e.g. counts), largest first with `SortOrder.Descending`. The first series with a sort decides for the whole chart. Time and number x ignore it.

#### `<ScatterSeries>` (`ScatterSeries<TItem>`)

Scatter series: a marker per point, for how two measures relate, e.g. delivery distance against delivery time. With `ScatterSeries.SizeValue` it is a bubble chart: a third measure sets each marker's size. The tooltip shows the point nearest the pointer.

- `MarkerSize`: `double?` — Marker diameter in pixels. Default 5. Bubbles: the diameter of the largest bubble; default from the chart size.
- `TrendLine`: `bool` — Draw a dashed least-squares trend line through the points.
- `SizeValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Each item's size, e.g. `c => c.Population`, which makes a bubble chart: a bubble's area is proportional to its size, and all bubble series in a chart share one size scale. Sizes of zero or less, or null, are not drawn. Aggregated points take the sum of their items' sizes.
- `SizeName`: `string?` — Bubbles: what the size is, shown with it in the tooltip, e.g. "Population". Default: "Size" in the chart's language.
- `SizeFormat`: `string?` — Bubbles: .NET format string for the size in tooltips, e.g. "0 M".
- `Error`: `double?` — Error bars: the same plus-or-minus amount for every point, e.g. 2.5.
- `ErrorValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Error bars: each item's plus-or-minus amount, e.g. `m => m.StdDev`; null for none. Items combined into one point take the average.
- `ErrorLowValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Error bars: the low end of each item's error bar (a value, e.g. a confidence interval's lower bound); use with `ErrorBarSeriesBase.ErrorHighValue`. Items combined into one point take the lowest.
- `ErrorHighValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Error bars: the high end of each item's error bar; use with `ErrorBarSeriesBase.ErrorLowValue`. Items combined into one point take the highest.

#### `<HeatmapSeries>` (`HeatmapSeries<TItem>`)

One row of a heatmap: its x values are the columns, its y values the cell colors (more opaque for higher values). Add one per row, e.g. per weekday; the Name labels the row. All rows share one color scale (the first row's Color, Format, Max, Midpoint and BelowColor).

- `Max`: `double?` — The value that gets the full color (e.g. 100 for percentages). Default: the highest value.
- `Midpoint`: `double?` — Colors diverge from this value, e.g. 0 for changes or 20 for °C: values above it take the series color, values below it `HeatmapSeries.BelowColor`, stronger the further they are from it. Default: one color, stronger for higher values.
- `BelowColor`: `string?` — With a `HeatmapSeries.Midpoint`: the color of values below it. Default `--rio-negative`.

#### `<RangeAreaSeries>` (`RangeAreaSeries<TItem>`)

Range area: a band between a low and a high value per x, e.g. the lowest and highest daily revenue around its average. Usually drawn behind a line; the tooltip shows "low – high".

- `LowValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — The low end of each point.
- `HighValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — The high end of each point (the same as `YValue`).
- `Curve`: `CurveType` — Line shape of the band's edges: Linear or Monotone.

#### `<BoxPlotSeries>` (`BoxPlotSeries<TItem>`)

Box plot: the spread of values per x, e.g. supply temperatures per unit. Give the raw values (`XValue` and `YValue`, one item per value: items with the same x form a box, with quartiles, whiskers at 1.5 × the box length and outliers computed here), or boxes computed elsewhere (`BoxPlotSeries.Q1Value`, `BoxPlotSeries.Q3Value` and the others, one item per box). Several box series sit side by side like grouped bars.

- `LowValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Precomputed boxes: the lower whisker end.
- `Q1Value`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Precomputed boxes: the lower quartile. With `BoxPlotSeries.Q3Value`, each item is one box.
- `MedianValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Precomputed boxes: the median (the same as `YValue`).
- `Q3Value`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Precomputed boxes: the upper quartile.
- `HighValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Precomputed boxes: the upper whisker end.
- `OutliersValue`: `Func<TItem, IEnumerable<double>?>?` — Precomputed boxes: values beyond the whiskers, drawn as dots (optional).
- `CountValue`: `Func<TItem, int?>?` — Precomputed boxes: how many values the box summarizes, for the tooltip (optional).

#### `<CandlestickSeries>` (`CandlestickSeries<TItem>`)

Candlestick: how a value moved within each period: a wick from low to high and a body from open to close, lightly filled when it rose and solid when it fell, in the series color (or green and red with `CandlestickSeries.DirectionColors`). Give raw readings (`XValue` and `YValue`, one item per reading) with a `CandlestickSeries.Bucket` such as an hour or a day, or candles computed elsewhere (`CandlestickSeries.OpenValue`, `CandlestickSeries.HighValue`, `CandlestickSeries.LowValue` and `CandlestickSeries.CloseValue`, one item per period). When zoomed out, candles too narrow to see merge into wider ones.

- `Bucket`: `TimeBucket?` — Raw readings: the period of each candle, e.g. `TimeBucket.Hour` (on the readings' wall-clock time, or in the chart's `TimeZone` when set); `TimeBucket.Auto` picks it from the data's time span (about 50 candles).
- `DirectionColors`: `bool` — Color candles by direction, rising in `--rio-positive` and falling in `--rio-negative` (green and red), with the change in percent in the tooltip, as for prices. Off (default): the series color, with a light fill for rising and a solid fill for falling candles.
- `OpenValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Precomputed candles: the period's first value.
- `HighValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Precomputed candles: the highest value.
- `LowValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Precomputed candles: the lowest value.
- `CloseValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Precomputed candles: the period's last value (the same as `YValue`).

#### `<BarSeries>` (`BarSeries<TItem>`)

Bar series. Several bar series in one chart are grouped side by side.

- `Bucket`: `TimeBucket?` — Time x: one point per bucket (e.g. `TimeBucket.Day` or `TimeBucket.Month`, on the items' wall-clock time, or in the chart's `TimeZone` when set) at the bucket's start, combining its items with `Aggregate` (average when not set) or `YAggregate`. `TimeBucket.Auto` picks the bucket from the data's time span (about 50 buckets).
- `MaxBarWidth`: `double?` — The widest a bar may be, in pixels. Default: as wide as its band allows, but a group of bars never takes more than a fifth of the plot (as with four categories), so a lone bar does not fill the chart. Bars stay centered on their band.
- `Sort`: `SortOrder?` — Category x: orders the categories by this series' values (after `Aggregate`, e.g. counts), largest first with `SortOrder.Descending`. The first series with a sort decides for the whole chart. Time and number x ignore it.
- `Error`: `double?` — Error bars: the same plus-or-minus amount for every point, e.g. 2.5.
- `ErrorValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Error bars: each item's plus-or-minus amount, e.g. `m => m.StdDev`; null for none. Items combined into one point take the average.
- `ErrorLowValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Error bars: the low end of each item's error bar (a value, e.g. a confidence interval's lower bound); use with `ErrorBarSeriesBase.ErrorHighValue`. Items combined into one point take the lowest.
- `ErrorHighValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Error bars: the high end of each item's error bar; use with `ErrorBarSeriesBase.ErrorLowValue`. Items combined into one point take the highest.

#### `<HistogramSeries>` (`HistogramSeries<TItem>`)

Histogram: how values are distributed, e.g. response times. Give one item per value: `XValue` is the value to count (a number). The values are counted in equal-width bins with round edges (`HistogramSeries.BinWidth` or `HistogramSeries.BinCount`, picked from the data when not set), drawn as bars that touch. The tooltip shows the bin's range and count; a click gives its items. Several histograms on one chart overlay, see-through.

- `BinWidth`: `double?` — The width of each bin, in x units (e.g. 5 for bins of 5 ms). Default: a nice width picked from the data.
- `BinCount`: `int?` — About how many bins, when `HistogramSeries.BinWidth` is not set (the width is rounded to a nice number). Default: picked from the data.

#### `<RangeBarSeries>` (`RangeBarSeries<TItem>`)

Range bars (a timeline): a bar from each item's `RangeBarSeries.StartValue` to its `RangeBarSeries.EndValue` (times, or numbers) in the row `RangeBarSeries.RowValue` gives, e.g. a project schedule (one row per task) or states over time (one row per machine). Rows are listed top to bottom in the order they first appear. Several range bar series share the rows and the time axis, so a state timeline is one series per state (running, idle, stopped), each with its color and legend entry. The tooltip shows the row, start, end and duration. Cannot be mixed with other series types; x lines and bands (`Annotations`) mark times such as "now".

- `RowValue`: `Func<TItem, string?>?` — The row of each item, e.g. `t => t.Machine`. Default: every bar in one row, named after the series.
- `StartValue`: `Func<TItem, object?>?` — Where each bar starts: a DateTime, DateTimeOffset, DateOnly or number. Items without a start are left out.
- `EndValue`: `Func<TItem, object?>?` — Where each bar ends, of the same kind as `RangeBarSeries.StartValue`. A missing end, or one before the start, draws nothing.

#### `<WaterfallSeries>` (`WaterfallSeries<TItem>`)

Waterfall: how a start value becomes an end value, e.g. a month's result from revenue through costs. Each item is a change (`YValue`), drawn as a bar from the running total before it to the one after: in `--rio-positive` (green) when it rises and `--rio-negative` (red) when it falls. Items marked with `WaterfallSeries.IsTotal` are totals: a bar from zero to the running total, in the series color. Thin lines carry each bar's end over to the next. The tooltip shows the change and the running total after it.

- `IsTotal`: `Func<TItem, bool>?` — Marks the totals, e.g. `s => s.IsTotal`: a total shows the running total so far, so its own `YValue` is ignored (it can return null). Totals in between (a subtotal) keep the running total going. Aggregated points are totals when their first item is.

#### `<FunnelSeries>` (`FunnelSeries<TItem>`)

Funnel: one segment per stage, top to bottom in the order of the items, each as wide at its top as its share of the largest stage and narrowing to the next, in a color of its own (one color when `Color` is set; `ColorValue` colors a stage). `XValue` is the stage, `YValue` how many reached it. Each stage shows its value and its share of the stage before (`DataLabels="false"` hides them), with its name in a column on the left; the tooltip adds the share of the first stage. One funnel per chart; it cannot be mixed with other series.

No parameters of its own.

#### `<CalendarSeries>` (`CalendarSeries<TItem>`)

Calendar heatmap: a square per day, weeks as columns and weekdays as rows, colored by the day's value like a heatmap (one hue, stronger for higher values; `Midpoint` makes it diverge). `XValue` is a date or time; items on the same day (in the chart's `TimeZone` when set) add up, or combine with `Aggregate`, and without a `YValue` each day counts its items. Up to a year of data is one block from the first day to the last; longer data is one block per year. The week starts on the chart culture's first day. One calendar per chart; it cannot be mixed with other series.

- `Max`: `double?` — The value that gets the full color (e.g. 100 for percentages). Default: the highest value.
- `Midpoint`: `double?` — Colors diverge from this value, e.g. 0 for changes or 20 for °C: days above it take the series color, days below it `CalendarSeries.BelowColor`, stronger the further they are from it. Default: one color, stronger for higher values.
- `BelowColor`: `string?` — With a `CalendarSeries.Midpoint`: the color of days below it. Default `--rio-negative`.

#### `<PieSeries>` (`PieSeries<TItem>`)

Pie: one slice per category (the x value), sized by its share of the total. Several pie series in one chart are drawn as nested rings, the first one outermost.

- `InnerRadius`: `double?` — Inner radius as a fraction of the outer radius; above 0 makes a donut. Default: 0 for one pie, 0.4 when several pie series are drawn as rings.
- `StartAngle`: `double?` — Start angle in degrees, clockwise from 12 o'clock. Default 0.
- `EndAngle`: `double?` — End angle in degrees. Default: a full circle. 180 with StartAngle -90 makes a half donut.
- `GroupSmallSlices`: `double?` — Group slices below this share of the total (e.g. 0.03) into one "Other" slice.

#### `<DonutSeries>` (`DonutSeries<TItem>`)

A pie with a hole (inner radius 0.6 by default); shows the total in the middle.

- `InnerRadius`: `double?` = `0.6` — Inner radius as a fraction of the outer radius; above 0 makes a donut. Default: 0 for one pie, 0.4 when several pie series are drawn as rings.
- `StartAngle`: `double?` — Start angle in degrees, clockwise from 12 o'clock. Default 0.
- `EndAngle`: `double?` — End angle in degrees. Default: a full circle. 180 with StartAngle -90 makes a half donut.
- `GroupSmallSlices`: `double?` — Group slices below this share of the total (e.g. 0.03) into one "Other" slice.

#### `<RadarSeries>` (`RadarSeries<TItem>`)

Radar: one spoke per category (x), clockwise from 12 o'clock, and a closed shape per series through its values. The radius is a linear scale from zero shared by all spokes; set the chart's `YAxis` Min and Max to fix it (e.g. 0 to 100 for percentages). Several radar series compare, e.g. two products' test scores against their class average. Cannot be mixed with other series types.

No parameters of its own.

#### `<TreemapSeries>` (`TreemapSeries<TItem>`)

Treemap: rectangles sized by value, nested by group, for how a total splits into many parts. `XValue` is each item's path from the outermost group, e.g. `"Europe/Sweden/Stockholm"` (see `TreemapSeries.PathSeparator`), or its name with `TreemapSeries.ParentValue`. A group's value is the sum of its items. Colors and legend items follow the top-level groups. Zero and negative values are left out. Cannot be mixed with other series types.

- `ParentValue`: `Func<TItem, object?>?` — The name of each item's group, matching another item's `XValue` (null or unknown: a top-level item). Builds the paths from a parent-child list, e.g. cities with their countries and countries with their regions; names must then be unique.
- `PathSeparator`: `string?` — What separates the groups in an `XValue` path. Default "/".
- `GroupSmallItems`: `double?` — Group items smaller than this share of their group (e.g. 0.03) into one "Other" item per group.
- `VisibleLevels`: `int?` — How many levels to draw at once below the group shown, e.g. 2 for continents and their countries; deeper groups show as one cell with their total and open on a click (drill-down). Null: all levels. The data keeps every level either way.

#### `<GaugeSeries>` (`GaugeSeries<TItem>`)

A gauge: a value on a scale from `GaugeSeries.Min` to `GaugeSeries.Max`, drawn as an arc with the value in the middle. Give one `GaugeSeries.Value`, or Items with `YValue` (and `XValue` for each gauge's label) for a row of gauges. `ColorBands` color the scale's ranges (and the value, when it is in one); `GaugeSeries.Target` marks a target.

- `Value`: `double?` — The value to show; used instead of Items when set. Its label is `Name`. A chart without items still needs a `TItem`, e.g. `<RioChart TItem="object">`.
- `Min`: `double?` — The value at the start of the scale. Default 0 (or a nice value below a negative value).
- `Max`: `double?` — The value at the end of the scale, e.g. 100 for percentages. Default: a nice value above the largest.
- `Target`: `double?` — A target value, marked across the scale and given in the tooltip.
- `InnerRadius`: `double?` — Inner radius as a fraction of the outer radius. Default 0.8.
- `StartAngle`: `double?` — Start angle in degrees, clockwise from 12 o'clock. Default -120 (with `GaugeSeries.EndAngle` 120); -90 and 90 make a half circle.
- `EndAngle`: `double?` — End angle in degrees. Default 120.

#### `<BulletSeries>` (`BulletSeries<TItem>`)

Bullets: each value as a bar on a horizontal scale from `BulletSeries.Min` to `BulletSeries.Max`, in a row of its own, over the scale's ranges (`ColorBands`, tinted) with a target mark. Give one `BulletSeries.Value`, or Items with `XValue` (each row's label) and `YValue`. Each series has its own scale, so measures in different units (revenue, margin, satisfaction) can be one series each in the same chart.

- `Value`: `double?` — The value to show; used instead of Items when set. Its label is `Name`. A chart without items still needs a `TItem`, e.g. `<RioChart TItem="object">`.
- `Min`: `double?` — The value at the start of the scale. Default 0 (or a nice value below a negative value).
- `Max`: `double?` — The value at the end of the scale. Default: a nice value above the largest value and target.
- `Target`: `double?` — A target for every row, marked across it and given in the tooltip. `BulletSeries.TargetValue` gives one per item.
- `TargetValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Each item's target, e.g. `k => k.Goal`; null for none (then `BulletSeries.Target`). Items combined into one row (`Aggregate`) get the same aggregate of their targets, or the average without one.

#### `<DumbbellSeries>` (`DumbbellSeries<TItem>`)

Dumbbells: two values per category joined by a line, e.g. before and after, or plan and actual. `DumbbellSeries.FromValue` is the first value (a hollow dot), `YValue` the second (a filled dot). `XValue` is the category; with `RioChart.Horizontal` the categories are rows, the classic layout. The tooltip shows "58 → 66 (+8)".

- `FromValue`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Each item's first value (before, plan), e.g. `c => c.LastYear`; null for none. Items combined into one point (`Aggregate`) get the same aggregate of their first values, or the average without one.

#### `<RadialBarSeries>` (`RadialBarSeries<TItem>`)

Radial bars: one circular track per category, filled up to its value.

- `Max`: `double?` — The value of a full track, e.g. 100 for percentages. Default: a nice value above the largest.
- `InnerRadius`: `double?` — Inner radius as a fraction of the outer radius. Default 0.3.
- `StartAngle`: `double?` — Start angle in degrees, clockwise from 12 o'clock. Default 0.
- `EndAngle`: `double?` — End angle in degrees. Default 270.

#### `<MapSeries>` (`MapSeries<TItem>`)

A world map: each country colored by its value, one hue that gets stronger with the value (a choropleth). `XValue` is the country: an ISO 3166 alpha-2 or alpha-3 code (`"SE"`, `"SWE"`) or English name; `YValue` its value. Several items for one country add up. Clicking a country zooms into it (see `RioChart.TreemapPath`), with a path bar back to the world. Combine with `MapBubbleSeries` for places within the countries. Cannot be mixed with other series types.

- `Max`: `double?` — The value given the strongest color, e.g. 100 for percentages. Default: the largest value.
- `Midpoint`: `double?` — Colors diverge from this value, e.g. 0 for growth: countries above it take the series color, those below it `MapSeries.BelowColor`, stronger the further they are from it. Default: one color, stronger for higher values.
- `BelowColor`: `string?` — With a `MapSeries.Midpoint`: the color of values below it. Default `--rio-negative`.

#### `<MapBubbleSeries>` (`MapBubbleSeries<TItem>`)

Bubbles on a world map: a circle at each item's `MapBubbleSeries.Latitude` and `MapBubbleSeries.Longitude`, its area proportional to `YValue` (e.g. users per city). `XValue` names the place in the tooltip. Items without a place, and values of zero or less, are not drawn. Draws on its own or on top of a `MapSeries`.

- `Latitude`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Each item's latitude in degrees north, e.g. `c => c.Latitude`.
- `Longitude`: `Func<TItem, double?>?` — Each item's longitude in degrees east, e.g. `c => c.Longitude`.
- `MarkerSize`: `double?` — The diameter of the largest bubble in pixels. Default: from the map's size.
- `GroupByCountry`: `bool?` — On the world map, one bubble per country with the sum of its places, so cities close together do not pile up; zoomed into a country, each place. Default true.

#### Parameters of every annotation (`AnnotationBase`)

Every annotation component below takes these, plus its own.

- `Id`: `string?` — Optional id, reported by `RioChart.OnAnnotationClick` and `OnAnnotationChanged`.
- `YAxisId`: `string?` — Vertical axis id for Y annotations, points and callouts. Default: the primary axis.
- `Label`: `string?` — Text shown next to the annotation.
- `Color`: `string?` — CSS color. Default: the muted annotation color (`--rio-annotation`).
- `ExpandsDomain`: `bool?` — Grow the axis range to include the annotation. Default: yes, except for bands.
- `Layer`: `AnnotationLayer?` — Draw below or above the series. Default: bands below, the rest above.

#### `<ReferenceLine>` (`ReferenceLine<TValue>`)

A horizontal (Axis="Y", default) or vertical (Axis="X") line, e.g. a target or "today". With `ReferenceLine.Draggable` the user can move it; bind the value with `@bind-Value`. `<ReferenceLine @bind-Value="limit" Label="Limit" Draggable="true" />`

- `Value`: `TValue` — Position in data units.
- `Axis`: `AnnotationAxis` = `AnnotationAxis.Y` — X for a vertical line; Y (default) for a horizontal one.
- `LabelPosition`: `LabelPosition?` — Where the label sits along the line. Default: End.
- `Draggable`: `bool` — Let the user drag the line; the new value goes to `ReferenceLine.ValueChanged`.
- `ValueChanged`: `EventCallback<TValue>` — Called with the new value when the user drags the line.

#### `<ReferenceBand>`

A range on the y axis (an acceptable zone) or the x axis (a period such as a fault). `<ReferenceBand Axis="AnnotationAxis.X" From="faultStart" To="faultEnd" Label="Fault" />`

- `From`: `object?` — Start of the range: a number, DateTime, DateTimeOffset, DateOnly or category name.
- `To`: `object?` — End of the range, in the same units as `ReferenceBand.From`.
- `Axis`: `AnnotationAxis` = `AnnotationAxis.Y` — X for a time period or category range; Y (default) for a value range.
- `LabelPosition`: `LabelPosition?` — Where the label sits. Default: Start.

#### `<PointAnnotation>`

A marker at a data point with an optional label above it, e.g. "Alarm". `<PointAnnotation X="alarmTime" Y="26.5" Label="Alarm" />`

- `X`: `object?` — The x value: a number, DateTime, DateTimeOffset, DateOnly or category name.
- `Y`: `double` — The y value on the annotation's vertical axis.

#### `<Callout>`

A text box with a connector line to a data point. `<Callout X="t" Y="18.2" Label="Filter changed" OffsetX="30" OffsetY="-40" />`

- `X`: `object?` — The x value of the point: a number, DateTime, DateTimeOffset, DateOnly or category name.
- `Y`: `double` — The y value of the point on the annotation's vertical axis.
- `OffsetX`: `double?` — Horizontal offset of the box from the point in pixels (negative: to the left). Default 24.
- `OffsetY`: `double?` — Vertical offset of the box from the point in pixels (negative: up). Default -32.

### Types used by parameters

#### `LegendClickingEventArgs` (class, RioCharts.Blazor)

Raised before a legend click shows or hides its series. Set `LegendClickingEventArgs.Cancel` to keep it as it is, e.g. to do something else instead (show only that series, open details).

- `SeriesId`: `string` — The clicked item's series id (or category, for pies).
- `Name`: `string` — The clicked item's name.
- `Visible`: `bool` — Whether the series is about to be shown (true) or hidden (false).
- `Cancel`: `bool` — Set to true to leave the series as it is.

#### `ExportFormats` (enum, RioCharts.Blazor)

The formats offered in the download menu (`Exportable`).

- `None` — No download menu.
- `Png` — PNG image.
- `Svg` — SVG document.
- `Csv` — The data as CSV.
- `All` — All formats.

Flags: combine values with `|`.

#### `ChartExportingEventArgs` (class, RioCharts.Blazor)

Raised when the user picks a format in the download menu, before the file is saved. Change `ChartExportingEventArgs.FileName` or the options, or set `ChartExportingEventArgs.Cancel` and handle the export yourself (e.g. upload it) with `ChartExportingEventArgs.GetPngAsync`, `ChartExportingEventArgs.GetSvgAsync` or `ChartExportingEventArgs.GetCsv`. The content is made only when one of those is called, so a handler that only renames costs nothing.

- `Format`: `ExportFormat` (read-only) — The format the user picked.
- `FileName`: `string` — The file name with extension; change it to save under another name.
- `ImageOptions`: `ChartImageOptions` — Options for PNG and SVG (used by the download and by GetPngAsync/GetSvgAsync).
- `CsvOptions`: `CsvOptions?` — Options for CSV; null: the defaults, with the x axis title as the x header.
- `Cancel`: `bool` — Set to true to skip the browser download (after handling the export yourself, or to block it).

- `Task<byte[]> GetPngAsync()` — The chart as PNG bytes, with `ChartExportingEventArgs.ImageOptions`.
- `Task<string> GetSvgAsync()` — The chart as an SVG document, with `ChartExportingEventArgs.ImageOptions`.
- `string GetCsv()` — The data as CSV, with `ChartExportingEventArgs.CsvOptions`.

#### `AxisOptions` (record, RioCharts.Core)

Settings for one axis: title, range, scale, label format and grid lines.

- `Id`: `string?` — Axis id that series and annotations refer to (vertical axes only). The primary vertical axis defaults to "y".
- `Title`: `string?` — Axis title.
- `Color`: `string?` — Vertical axes: CSS color of the tick labels and title, e.g. to show which axis belongs to which line. Null: the muted axis color (or the series color with `AxisOptions.SeriesColor`).
- `SeriesColor`: `bool` — Vertical axes: color the tick labels and title like the first visible series on the axis, so with one axis per series each axis matches its line. `AxisOptions.Color` wins when both are set.
- `TooltipFormat`: `string?` — X axis: .NET format string for the x value in tooltip headers only, e.g. "HH:mm" or "d MMM HH:mm". Unlike `AxisOptions.Format` it leaves the axis labels alone, and on a time axis it also leaves out the time zone offset that tooltips otherwise add when the chart's zone differs from the viewer's. Null: automatic.
- `Min`: `double?` — Fixed minimum. When null it comes from the data.
- `Max`: `double?` — Fixed maximum. When null it comes from the data.
- `Scale`: `ScaleType` — Scale type. Auto picks from the data: times give a time axis, numbers a linear axis, strings a band axis.
- `Format`: `string?` — .NET format string for labels, e.g. "P0", "C0" or "yyyy-MM-dd". Null for automatic formatting.
- `GridLines`: `bool?` — Draw grid lines. Null uses the default: on for the primary vertical axis, off otherwise.
- `LabelRotation`: `double?` — Angle of category labels on the x axis, in degrees from 0 to 90; they slope down to the left. Null (the default): horizontal when every label fits, otherwise 45 degrees. 0 keeps them horizontal and shows every n-th label when they do not all fit. Rotated labels still thin out when even they overlap.
- `Position`: `AxisPosition` — Side of a vertical axis. Auto: the primary axis on the left, additional axes on the right.
- `Stacking`: `StackMode` — How stacked series on a vertical axis add up. Percent: each stack fills the axis (0–100 %), so the series show their share per x value; line, area and bar series without a stack name are stacked together.

#### `LegendOptions` (record, RioCharts.Core)

Legend settings: when to show it and where.

- `Mode`: `LegendMode` — Auto shows the legend only when there is more than one series.
- `Position`: `LegendPosition` — Where the legend sits. Default Top.
- `Sizes`: `bool?` — Bubble charts: a size legend right of the plot, with circles for a few round sizes. Null: shown when the chart is at least 360 px wide and has room for a legend.

#### `TooltipOptions` (record, RioCharts.Core)

Tooltip settings.

- `Enabled`: `bool` = `true` — Show a tooltip and crosshair when hovering the plot.
- `Shared`: `bool` = `true` — True: one tooltip per x position listing every series. False: only the nearest point.

#### `TooltipPoint<TItem>` (record, RioCharts.Blazor)

One point in a tooltip: what `TooltipValue`, `TooltipHeader` and the rows of a `TooltipTemplate` get.

- `SeriesId`: `string` — Id of the series.
- `SeriesName`: `string` — Name of the series (as in the legend).
- `Color`: `string` — The series color as a CSS color, e.g. for a dot in a template.
- `Index`: `int` — Index into the series' input (items list or columns); the first item's when the series aggregates; -1 for a grouped "Other" slice.
- `X`: `object?` — The x value: a number, DateTime (DateTimeOffset with a display time zone) or category name.
- `Y`: `double` — The y value (the series' own value, also when stacked); NaN for a gap or an "Other" slice.
- `XText`: `string` — The x value as the tooltip header shows it by default (the category for pie slices).
- `ValueText`: `string` — The value as the tooltip shows it: formatted with the series' `Format`, or the series' `TooltipValue`.
- `Item`: `TItem` — The input item (the first of the group when the series aggregates), or default for columnar data.
- `Items`: `IReadOnlyList<TItem>` — All input items behind the point: the group when the series aggregates; empty for columnar data.

- `new TooltipPoint(string SeriesId, string SeriesName, string Color, int Index, object? X, double Y, string XText, string ValueText)` — One point in a tooltip: what `TooltipValue`, `TooltipHeader` and the rows of a `TooltipTemplate` get.

#### `TooltipContext<TItem>` (record, RioCharts.Blazor)

What a `TooltipTemplate` renders: the hovered x and one point per listed series.

- `Header`: `string` — The default header text (the formatted x, or `TooltipHeader`); the series name for nested pies.
- `X`: `object?` — The hovered x value (the first point's).
- `Points`: `IReadOnlyList<TooltipPoint<TItem>>` — The listed points in tooltip order: one per series for a shared tooltip, else one.

- `new TooltipContext(string Header, object? X, IReadOnlyList<TooltipPoint<TItem>> Points)` — What a `TooltipTemplate` renders: the hovered x and one point per listed series.

#### `Annotation` (record, RioCharts.Core)

A reference line or band. Values are in data units of the axis: numbers, times (DateTime, DateTimeOffset, DateOnly or an ISO 8601 string) or category names.

- `Id`: `string?` — Optional id, reported in click events.
- `Type`: `AnnotationType` — Kind of annotation: a line, a band, a point or a callout. Default Line.
- `Axis`: `AnnotationAxis` = `AnnotationAxis.Y` — Axis the value(s) refer to: Y for a horizontal line or band, X for a vertical one.
- `YAxisId`: `string?` — Vertical axis id for Y annotations. Null uses the primary axis.
- `Value`: `object?` — Position of a line: a number, a time (ISO 8601) or a category.
- `From`: `object?` — Start of a band.
- `To`: `object?` — End of a band.
- `X`: `object?` — Point and callout: the x value (a number, a time or a category).
- `Y`: `object?` — Point and callout: the y value on the annotation's vertical axis.
- `OffsetX`: `double?` — Callout: horizontal offset of the text box from the point, in pixels. Default 24.
- `OffsetY`: `double?` — Callout: vertical offset of the text box from the point, in pixels (negative is up). Default -32.
- `Draggable`: `bool` — Line: the user can drag it to a new value (e.g. to edit a threshold); the chart reports the new value.
- `Label`: `string?` — Optional label.
- `LabelPosition`: `LabelPosition?` — Where the label sits along the line or band. Default: End for lines, Start for bands.
- `Color`: `string?` — CSS color. Null uses the muted annotation color.
- `ExpandsDomain`: `bool?` — Whether the axis range grows to include the annotation. Default: true for lines, false for bands.
- `Layer`: `AnnotationLayer?` — Draw below or above the series. Default: bands below, lines above.

#### `UnspecifiedTimes` (enum, RioCharts.Core.Data)

How times without a zone (DateTime with Kind Unspecified, DateOnly, plain strings) are read when a display zone is set.

- `Utc` — They are UTC.
- `DisplayZone` — They are wall-clock times in the display zone.

#### `ChartTexts` (record, RioCharts.Core)

The texts a chart shows or reads out itself: empty states, the legend and axis names for screen readers, the chart description, "Reset zoom", the download menu and the keyboard help. Your own texts (titles, series names, formats) are not here.

84 properties: `Chart`, `NoData`, `AllSeriesHidden`, `AllSlicesHidden`, `Other`, `Total`, `Size`, `ResetZoom`, `Download`, `DownloadFormat`, `DownloadChart`, `ChartRole`, `Legend`, `XAxis`, `YAxis`, `AxisRange`, `SeriesPoints`, `Summary`, `SummaryTitled`, `SeriesValues`, `LowestHighest`, `Trend`, `Rising`, `Falling`, `Stable`, `ValueRange`, `LastValue`, `HistogramPeak`, `RangeBarSummary`, `DurationUnits`, `BoxMax`, `BoxUpperQuartile`, `BoxMedian`, `BoxLowerQuartile`, `BoxMin`, `BoxCount`, `BoxOutliers`, `CandleOpen`, `CandleHigh`, `CandleLow`, `CandleClose`, `CandleChange`, `NoDataShort`, `PieChart`, `DonutChart`, `RadialBarChart`, `GaugeChart`, `BulletChart`, `FunnelChart`, `FunnelOfFirst`, `FunnelOfPrevious`, `CalendarChart`, `CalendarDays`, `Target`, `RadarChart`, `Treemap`, `ShareOfGroup`, `ShareOfTotal`, `TreemapAll`, `TreemapShow`, `TreemapPathLabel`, `Map`, `MapWorld`, `TreemapLeftOut`, `PolarItems`, `PolarNoData`, `More`, `KeysPoints`, `KeysPointsAndSeries`, `KeysSlices`, `KeysZoom`, `KeysSelect`, `KeysLeave`, `Position`, `Keys`, `English`, `Swedish`, `Norwegian`, `Danish`, `Finnish`, `German`, `French`, `Spanish`, `BuiltIn`.

- `static void Register(string culture, ChartTexts texts)` — Adds or replaces the texts for a culture or language ("pl", "pt-BR"), for every chart in the app. Call it at startup. Takes precedence over the built-in languages.
- `static ChartTexts For(CultureInfo? culture)` — The texts for a culture: registered ones, then built-in ones, trying the culture and its parents (sv-FI, then sv); English when none match. Null: the current UI culture.
- `static ChartTexts From(Func<string, string?> lookup, ChartTexts? fallback = null)` — Texts from a lookup by key (see `ChartTexts.Keys`), e.g. resx resources or an IStringLocalizer: `ChartTexts.From(key => localizer[key] is { ResourceNotFound: false } s ? s.Value : null)`. Keys it returns null or empty for keep the text from `fallback` (default English).
- `string Fill(string key, IFormatProvider? provider, object?[] args)` — Fills in this set's template for `key` (a property name, see `ChartTexts.Keys`) with `args`, the way charts do. Never throws: a template that cannot be filled falls back to the English one.

#### `LegendClickEventArgs` (record, RioCharts.Blazor)

Raised when a legend item is clicked (the series has already been toggled).

- `SeriesId`: `string`
- `Name`: `string`
- `Visible`: `bool`

- `new LegendClickEventArgs(string SeriesId, string Name, bool Visible)` — Raised when a legend item is clicked (the series has already been toggled).

#### `PointClickEventArgs<TItem>` (record, RioCharts.Blazor)

Raised when a point or bar is clicked.

- `SeriesId`: `string`
- `SeriesName`: `string`
- `Item`: `TItem` — The input item (the first of the group when the series aggregates), or default for columnar data.
- `Index`: `int` — Index into the series' input (items list or columns); the first item's when the series aggregates.
- `X`: `object?` — The x value: a number, DateTime or category name.
- `Y`: `double` — The y value (the series' own value, also when stacked).
- `Items`: `IReadOnlyList<TItem>` — All input items behind the point: the group when the series aggregates (`Aggregate` or `YAggregate`), else just `PointClickEventArgs.Item`; empty for columnar data.

- `new PointClickEventArgs(string SeriesId, string SeriesName, TItem Item, int Index, object? X, double Y)` — Raised when a point or bar is clicked.

#### `AnnotationClickEventArgs` (record, RioCharts.Blazor)

Raised when a reference line or band is clicked.

- `AnnotationId`: `string` — The annotation's `Id`.
- `Label`: `string?` — The annotation's label.

- `new AnnotationClickEventArgs(string AnnotationId, string? Label)` — Raised when a reference line or band is clicked.

#### `AnnotationChangedEventArgs` (record, RioCharts.Blazor)

Raised when the user has dragged a reference line to a new value.

- `AnnotationId`: `string` — The annotation's `Id`.
- `Label`: `string?` — The annotation's label.
- `Value`: `object` — The new value: DateTime on time axes, else double.

- `new AnnotationChangedEventArgs(string AnnotationId, string? Label, object Value)` — Raised when the user has dragged a reference line to a new value.

#### `ChartRange` (record, RioCharts.Blazor)

A range on the x axis (the visible window when zoomed). Values are `DateTime` on time axes and `Double` on numeric axes; DateTimeOffset, DateOnly and numbers are accepted as input.

- `Min`: `object` — Start of the range.
- `Max`: `object` — End of the range.

- `new ChartRange(object Min, object Max)` — A range on the x axis (the visible window when zoomed). Values are `DateTime` on time axes and `Double` on numeric axes; DateTimeOffset, DateOnly and numbers are accepted as input.
- `static ChartRange Of(DateTime min, DateTime max)` — A range on a time axis.
- `static ChartRange Of(double min, double max)` — A range on a numeric axis.

#### `ZoomChangingEventArgs` (class, RioCharts.Blazor)

Raised before a zoom or pan is applied. Change `ZoomChangingEventArgs.Range` to clamp it, or set `ZoomChangingEventArgs.Cancel` to keep the current view. `ZoomChangingEventArgs.Range` is null for a reset.

- `Range`: `ChartRange?` — The range about to be shown; null when the zoom is reset.
- `Cancel`: `bool` — Set to true to keep the current view.

#### `SeriesLayer` (enum, RioCharts.Blazor)

Where the chart draws its series.

- `Svg` — SVG elements (default): crisp, styleable, one path per series.
- `Canvas` — A canvas over the SVG: no DOM per series, for many or dense series. Axes, labels and annotations stay SVG.

#### `MapProjection` (enum, RioCharts.Core)

How a map draws the round world flat.

- `EqualEarth` — Equal Earth: equal-area, so every country keeps its true relative size; the outline of the world is rounded.
- `Mercator` — Mercator, as on web maps: familiar shapes on a rectangle, but areas grow toward the poles; cut at ±85° latitude.

#### `ChartDefinition` (record, RioCharts.Core)

The chart model. Plain, serializable data: Razor components and (later) JSON definitions both compile to this. Data is not part of the definition; it is passed separately by series id.

- `Title`: `string?` — Optional chart title.
- `Compact`: `bool` — Compact chart (sparkline): no axes, grid, legend or title; the series fill the box and the y range fits the data tightly (bars keep zero). For small charts in tables and tiles.
- `AutoCompact`: `bool` = `true` — Default true: as the chart gets small, leave out axis titles, then the legend, title and axis labels; very small charts become compact. False keeps everything at any size.
- `Horizontal`: `bool` — Bar, box plot, waterfall and dumbbell charts: they run left to right with the categories down the side (first on top). For rankings and long category names. The y axis settings (title, format, min, max) apply to the values.
- `Projection`: `MapProjection` — Maps: how the round world is drawn flat. EqualEarth (default) keeps every country's true relative size; Mercator is the projection of web maps, familiar shapes but areas that grow toward the poles.
- `X`: `AxisOptions` — Horizontal axis.
- `Y`: `AxisOptions` — Primary vertical axis (id "y" unless set). Drawn on the left and owns the grid lines.
- `YAxes`: `IReadOnlyList<AxisOptions>` — Additional vertical axes, e.g. a second unit. Drawn on the right unless Position is Left. Series bind to them with yAxisId.
- `Legend`: `LegendOptions` — Legend settings. By default it is shown only when there is more than one series.
- `Tooltip`: `TooltipOptions` — Tooltip settings. On by default, with one tooltip per x position across series.
- `Series`: `IReadOnlyList<SeriesOptions>` — Series to draw, in order. Colors are assigned from the palette in this order.
