- `Annotations`: `IReadOnlyList<Annotation>` — Reference lines and bands, e.g. a target or an incident period.
- `TimeZone`: `string?` — Display time zone: "UTC", "local" (the viewer's zone) or an IANA id such as "Europe/Stockholm". Null shows times as given. Times are then plotted on instants and labelled in this zone.
- `UnspecifiedTimes`: `UnspecifiedTimes?` — With a display zone: how to read times without a zone (DateTime with Kind Unspecified). Utc or DisplayZone.
- `Dataset`: `string?` — Dataset (by id from the data source) that series read their x and y fields from, unless a series names its own.
- `Data`: `IReadOnlyList<IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?>>?` — Inline rows for small data, e.g. [{"month":"Jan","revenue":42}]. At most 1000 rows; prefer a dataset id for real data.

#### `ChartDataset` (class, RioCharts.Core.Definitions)

Tabular data that chart definitions refer to by name and fields, so a definition (e.g. from an AI agent) stays small and never has to carry the data itself.

- `Name`: `string` (read-only) — The name definitions refer to (matched case-insensitively).
- `Description`: `string?` (read-only) — What the data is (shown to AI agents), e.g. "Orders per day and store".
- `Fields`: `IReadOnlyList<DataField>` (read-only) — The columns.
- `RowCount`: `int` (read-only) — The number of rows (the longest field).

- `new ChartDataset(string name, IReadOnlyList<DataField> fields, string? description = null)` — Creates a dataset.
- `DataField? Field(string name)` — The field with this name (case-insensitive), or null.
- `static ChartDataset FromRows(string name, IEnumerable<IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?>> rows, string? description = null, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? fieldDescriptions = null)` — Builds a dataset from rows of field values (numbers, times, text; JSON elements are read too).
- `static ChartDataset FromItems<T>(string name, IEnumerable<T> items, string? description = null, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? fieldDescriptions = null)` — Builds a dataset from objects: one field per public readable property (camelCase names).
- `static ChartDataset FromJson(string name, JsonElement array, string? description = null)` — Builds a dataset from a JSON array of objects.
- `static ChartDataset FromCsv(string name, string csv, string? description = null, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? fieldDescriptions = null)` — Builds a dataset from CSV text with a header row. The delimiter (comma, semicolon or tab) is detected from the header. Quoted cells may hold delimiters, quotes ("") and line breaks. Numbers use a decimal point; with a semicolon or tab delimiter a decimal comma also works (as Excel writes in many locales). ISO 8601 cells become times, empty cells are gaps.

#### `SelectionMode` (enum, RioCharts.Blazor)

What the user can select on a chart with the pointer or keyboard.

- `None` — Nothing (default). Selections set from code still show.
- `Points` — Points and bars: a click (or Enter on a focused point) selects one, Ctrl/Cmd or Shift+click adds or removes one, a click on an empty part of the plot clears the selection.
- `Range` — An x range: drag across the plot (mouse). A click without a drag clears it. With `Zoomable`, drag selects; zoom with Ctrl/Cmd+wheel, pinch or the keyboard instead.

#### `SelectionChangedEventArgs<TItem>` (record, RioCharts.Blazor)

Raised when the selection changes, by the user or from code.

- `Items`: `IReadOnlyList<TItem>` — The selected items: the selected points' items, or with a range the items of the visible series' points inside it. Empty for columnar data.
- `Range`: `ChartRange?` — The selected x range, or null when points (or nothing) are selected.

- `new SelectionChangedEventArgs(IReadOnlyList<TItem> Items, ChartRange? Range)` — Raised when the selection changes, by the user or from code.

#### `ChartImageOptions` (record, RioCharts.Blazor)

Options for exporting a chart as an image in the browser.

- `Scale`: `double` = `2` — PNG only: pixels per CSS pixel. Default 2 (sharp on high-density screens and in print).
- `Background`: `string?` — Background color (any CSS color). Default: the chart's surface color (`--rio-surface`), so the image reads the same outside the page. "transparent" for none.

#### `CsvOptions` (record, RioCharts.Core.Data)

Options for `ChartCsv.Write`.

- `Delimiter`: `Char` — Column separator. Default ','.
- `Culture`: `CultureInfo` — Culture for numbers. Default invariant (a '.' decimal point), which spreadsheets and code read alike.
- `XHeader`: `string` = `"x"` — Header of the x column. Default "x".
- `NewLine`: `string` = `"\r\n"` — Line ending. Default "\r\n" (RFC 4180).

#### `Aggregate` (enum, RioCharts.Core)

How rows with the same x (or time bucket) are combined into one value.

- `Sum` — The sum of the values.
- `Average` — The mean of the values.
- `Min` — The lowest value.
- `Max` — The highest value.
- `Count` — The number of rows (no y field needed).
- `Last` — The last value in row order, skipping missing values.

#### `SeriesData` (class, RioCharts.Core.Data)

The single data representation inside Core: contiguous columns (structure of arrays). `SeriesData.Y` uses NaN for missing values, which become gaps in lines. Numeric and time data is sorted by x on creation; `SeriesData.SourceIndex` maps back to the input.

- `X`: `double[]` (read-only) — The x values, sorted ascending: numbers, time in milliseconds (see `TimeValue`) or category indexes. Treat as read-only; the arrays are exposed for speed.
- `Y`: `double[]` (read-only) — The y values, one per x; NaN is a gap. Treat as read-only.
- `Kind`: `XKind` (read-only) — What the x values are: numbers, times or categories.
- `Count`: `int` (read-only) — The number of points.
- `Categories`: `IReadOnlyList<string>` (read-only) — Category names when `SeriesData.Kind` is Category; X holds indexes into this list.
- `SourceIndex`: `int[]?` (read-only) — For each point, its index in the original input; null when the input order was kept.
- `Low`: `double[]?` (read-only) — Range series: the low value of each point (`SeriesData.Y` is the high value), NaN where missing; null for other series. Set with `SeriesData.WithLow`.
- `Colors`: `string?[]?` (read-only) — Each point's own color (a CSS color or theme token such as "--rio-negative"), null where the point keeps its series color; null when no point has one. Set with `SeriesData.WithColors`.
- `Latitudes`: `double[]?` (read-only) — Map bubbles: each point's latitude in degrees, NaN where missing; null for other series. Set with `SeriesData.WithLocations`.
- `Longitudes`: `double[]?` (read-only) — Map bubbles: each point's longitude in degrees, NaN where missing; null for other series. Set with `SeriesData.WithLocations`.
- `Totals`: `bool[]?` (read-only) — Waterfalls: true for each total point, whose y is the running total of the changes before it; null for other series (and for a waterfall without totals). Set with `SeriesData.WithTotals`.
- `Sizes`: `double[]?` (read-only) — Bubbles (scatter with a size): each point's size, NaN where missing; null for other series. A bubble's area is proportional to its size. Set with `SeriesData.WithSizes`.
- `ErrorLow`: `double[]?` (read-only) — Error bars: the low end of each point's error bar (a value, not a distance), NaN where it has none; null when the series has no error bars. Set with `SeriesData.WithErrors`.
- `ErrorHigh`: `double[]?` (read-only) — Error bars: the high end of each point's error bar, NaN where it has none; null without error bars.
- `Targets`: `double[]?` (read-only) — Bullets: each point's target value, NaN where it has none; null for other series. Set with `SeriesData.WithTargets`.
- `Candles`: `CandleColumns?` (read-only) — Candlesticks: the open, high and low of each point (`SeriesData.Y` is the close); null for other series. Set with `SeriesData.WithCandles`.
- `Box`: `BoxColumns?` (read-only) — Box plots: the quartiles, whiskers, extremes and outliers of each point (`SeriesData.Y` is the median); null for other series. Set with `SeriesData.WithBox`.
- `TimeOffsets`: `double[]?` (read-only) — Time data: the UTC offset (milliseconds) of each point when the input had one (DateTimeOffset, or DateTime with Kind Utc or Local), NaN otherwise; null when no point had one. Used only when the chart has a display time zone; by default times are shown as given.
- `Rows`: `string[]?` (read-only) — Range bars: the row of each point, e.g. the machine or task it belongs to (`SeriesData.X` is the start, `SeriesData.Y` the end, in the same units); null for other series. Set with `SeriesData.WithRows` or made by `SeriesData.FromRanges`.
- `Empty`: `SeriesData` (static) — A series with no points.

- `SeriesData WithColors(IReadOnlyList<string?> colors)` — The same points with a color each (bars, scatter markers, slices, treemap items; a dot on lines and areas). `colors` is in input order like the y values: index i is the color of input item (or group) i; null keeps the series color.
- `SeriesData WithLocations(ReadOnlySpan<double> latitudes, ReadOnlySpan<double> longitudes)` — The same points with a place each, for bubbles on a map. Both are in input order, like the y values given when creating the data: index i is the place of input item (or group) i.
- `string ColorAt(int point, string fallback)` — The color of a point: its own, or `fallback` (the series color).
- `SeriesData WithLow(ReadOnlySpan<double> low)` — The same points with a low value each, for range series (`SeriesData.Y` is the high value). `low` is in input order, like the y values given when creating the data: index i is the low of input item (or column entry) i.
- `SeriesData WithTotals(ReadOnlySpan<bool> totals)` — The same points as a waterfall with totals: `totals` is in input order, like the y values given when creating the data (index i is true when input item or group i is a total). A total point's y becomes the running total of the changes before it (its own y is ignored); the other points are changes, and gaps (NaN) change nothing.
- `SeriesData WithSizes(ReadOnlySpan<double> sizes)` — The same points with a size each, which makes a scatter series a bubble chart. `sizes` is in input order, like the y values given when creating the data: index i is the size of input item (or group) i.
- `SeriesData WithErrors(ReadOnlySpan<double> low, ReadOnlySpan<double> high)` — The same points with an error bar each, from `low` to `high` (values on the y axis, e.g. y - sd and y + sd). Both are in input order, like the y values given when creating the data: index i belongs to input item (or group) i; NaN for none.
- `SeriesData WithTargets(ReadOnlySpan<double> targets)` — The same points with a target each (bullet charts). `targets` is in input order, like the y values given when creating the data: index i is the target of input item (or group) i.
- `SeriesData WithCandles(ReadOnlySpan<CandleSummary> candles)` — The same points as candles: `candles` is in input order (index i is the candle of input item or group i). Each point's y becomes its candle's close; an incomplete candle is a gap.
- `static SeriesData FromCandleBuckets<TItem>(IEnumerable<TItem> items, Func<TItem, object?> time, Func<TItem, double?> value, TimeBucket bucket, IReadOnlyList<int[]> groups, TimeConversion? zone = null)` — Candles from raw readings: the items are grouped per time bucket (e.g. per hour or day, on their wall-clock time, or in `zone` when set) and each bucket gives the first, highest, lowest and last value in time order. Null values are skipped.
- `static SeriesData FromTimeBuckets<TItem>(IEnumerable<TItem> items, Func<TItem, object?> time, TimeBucket bucket, Func<IReadOnlyList<TItem>, double?> aggregate, IReadOnlyList<int[]> groups, TimeConversion? zone = null)` — Groups items per time bucket (e.g. per day or month, on their wall-clock time, or in `zone` when set) and makes one point per bucket at the bucket's start, with y from `aggregate` (null is a gap). `TimeBucket.Auto` picks the bucket from the span of the times. Items with a null x are left out; x values that are not times group by value. Selectors and the aggregate run once here, never per render.
- `SeriesData WithBox(ReadOnlySpan<BoxSummary> boxes)` — The same points as boxes: `boxes` is in input order, like the y values given when creating the data (index i is the box of input item or group i). Each point's y becomes its box's median.
- `static SeriesData FromBoxGroups<TItem>(IEnumerable<TItem> items, Func<TItem, object?> xValue, Func<TItem, double?> value, IReadOnlyList<int[]> groups)` — Box plot data from raw values: items with the same x form one box, summarized with `BoxSummary.FromValues`. Categories keep the order of first appearance; numbers and times are sorted. Null values are skipped.
- `SeriesData WithRows(IReadOnlyList<string?> rows)` — The same points as range bars, each in a row: `rows` is in input order, like the y values given when creating the data (index i is the row of input item i); a null or missing row is "". `SeriesData.X` is each bar's start and `SeriesData.Y` its end.
- `static SeriesData FromRanges<TItem>(IEnumerable<TItem> items, Func<TItem, string?>? row, Func<TItem, object?> start, Func<TItem, object?> end)` — Range bars from items: a bar from `start` to `end` (both numbers, or both DateTime, DateTimeOffset or DateOnly; the first non-null start decides) in the row `row` gives (null: every bar in one row, named after the series). Items without a start are left out; a missing end, or one before the start, draws nothing. Points are sorted by start; selectors run once here, never per render.
- `int ToSourceIndex(int index)` — Index of the point in the original input (items list or columns).
- `static SeriesData From(ReadOnlySpan<double> x, ReadOnlySpan<double> y)` — Numeric x and y columns (copied). Points without a finite x are dropped, unsorted x is sorted, and missing y values are NaN (gaps).
- `static SeriesData From(ReadOnlyMemory<double> x, ReadOnlyMemory<double> y)` — Numeric x and y columns (copied).
- `static SeriesData From(ReadOnlySpan<DateTime> x, ReadOnlySpan<double> y)` — Time x and y columns (copied); times are used as given, see `TimeValue`.
- `static SeriesData From(ReadOnlyMemory<DateTime> x, ReadOnlyMemory<double> y)` — Time x and y columns (copied).
- `static SeriesData From(ReadOnlySpan<DateTimeOffset> x, ReadOnlySpan<double> y)` — Time x and y columns (copied); each value contributes its own wall-clock time.
- `static SeriesData From(ReadOnlyMemory<DateTimeOffset> x, ReadOnlyMemory<double> y)` — Time x and y columns (copied).
- `static SeriesData FromCategories(IReadOnlyList<string> categories, ReadOnlySpan<double> y)` — Category data; order of first appearance is kept.
- `static SeriesData FromItems<TItem>(IEnumerable<TItem> items, Func<TItem, object?> xValue, Func<TItem, double?> yValue)` — Builds columns from items. X may be a number, DateTime, DateTimeOffset, DateOnly or string (category); the first non-null value decides the kind. A null Y is a gap. Selectors run once here, never per render.
- `static SeriesData FromBins<TItem>(IEnumerable<TItem> items, Func<TItem, double?> value, double? width, int? count, IReadOnlyList<int[]> groups, Bins bins)` — A histogram: the items' values (`value`; null and NaN are skipped) counted in equal-width bins (`Bins.For`). One point per bin, empty bins included: x is the bin's middle, y the number of values in it. Selectors run once here, never per render.
- `static SeriesData FromGroups<TItem>(IEnumerable<TItem> items, Func<TItem, object?> xValue, Func<IReadOnlyList<TItem>, double?> aggregate)`
- `static SeriesData FromGroups<TItem>(IEnumerable<TItem> items, Func<TItem, object?> xValue, Func<IReadOnlyList<TItem>, double?> aggregate, IReadOnlyList<int[]> groups)` — Groups items with the same x and makes one point per group, with y from `aggregate` (null is a gap). Categories keep the order of first appearance; numbers and times are sorted as usual. Items with a null x are left out. Selectors and the aggregate run once here, never per render.

#### `ColorBand` (record, RioCharts.Core)

A color for values in a range, e.g. { "above": 120, "color": "--rio-negative" }: a line or area takes it where it runs in the range, a bar or scatter point when its value is in it.

- `Above`: `double?` — Values above this take the color. Null: no lower bound.
- `Below`: `double?` — Values below this take the color. Null: no upper bound.
- `Color`: `string` — A CSS color or a theme token such as "--rio-negative".

#### `SeriesBuffer` (class, RioCharts.Core.Data)

A growing window of points for live data: append from any thread, and charts that use it redraw at a capped rate. The oldest points drop out when `SeriesBuffer.Capacity` is reached or, for time data, when they are older than `SeriesBuffer.TimeWindow` behind the newest point.

- `Capacity`: `int` (read-only) — The most points kept; the oldest drop out beyond it.
- `TimeWindow`: `TimeSpan?` (read-only) — For time data: points further than this behind the newest one drop out. Null keeps them until `SeriesBuffer.Capacity`.
- `Kind`: `XKind` (read-only) — Time or Numeric x values.
- `Version`: `long` (read-only) — Increases with every change; charts compare it to know when to redraw.
- `Count`: `int` (read-only) — The number of points in the buffer now.

- `new SeriesBuffer(int capacity = 100000, TimeSpan? timeWindow = null, XKind kind = XKind.Time)`
- `void Append(DateTime x, double y)` — Appends a point at a time (used as given, see `TimeValue`). Thread-safe.
- `void Append(DateTimeOffset x, double y)` — Appends a point at a time (its own wall-clock time). Thread-safe.
- `void Append(double x, double y)` — Appends a point; y may be NaN for a gap. On time buffers x is in milliseconds (`TimeValue`).
- `void AppendRange(ReadOnlySpan<DateTime> x, ReadOnlySpan<double> y)` — Appends many points with one change notification.
- `void AppendRange(ReadOnlySpan<double> x, ReadOnlySpan<double> y)` — Appends many points with one change notification (x in data units).
- `void Clear()` — Removes all points. Thread-safe.
- `SeriesData ToSeriesData()` — A copy of the current points as chart data (sorted by x).

#### `TimeBucket` (enum, RioCharts.Core)

Time interval that rows are grouped into before aggregating.

- `Minute` — One bucket per minute.
- `Hour` — One bucket per hour.
- `Day` — One bucket per day.
- `Week` — One bucket per week, starting on Monday.
- `Month` — One bucket per calendar month.
- `Quarter` — One bucket per calendar quarter.
- `Year` — One bucket per calendar year.
- `Auto` — Picks one of the others from the data's time span: the one that gives closest to 50 buckets (e.g. weeks for a year of data, hours for a day). Chosen once per data change.

#### `CurveType` (enum, RioCharts.Core)

Line shape. Step holds each value until the next point.

- `Linear` — Straight segments between points.
- `Monotone` — A smooth curve that does not overshoot the data.
- `Step` — Holds each value until the next point.

#### `PointHighlight` (enum, RioCharts.Core)

Points of a line or area series to mark with a dot (combine with |).

- `None` — No highlighted points.
- `Last` — The last value (the latest, for time series).
- `First` — The first value.
- `Min` — The lowest value.
- `Max` — The highest value.
- `All` — Every point: shows where the values are when there are few of them.

Flags: combine values with `|`.

#### `SortOrder` (enum, RioCharts.Core)

Order of points sorted by value.

- `Ascending` — Smallest first.
- `Descending` — Largest first.

#### `AnnotationLayer` (enum, RioCharts.Core)

Whether an annotation is drawn below or above the series.

- `Below` — Behind the series.
- `Above` — On top of the series.

#### `AnnotationAxis` (enum, RioCharts.Core)

The axis a line or band annotation refers to.

- `X` — The horizontal axis: a vertical line or band.
- `Y` — A vertical axis: a horizontal line or band.

#### `LabelPosition` (enum, RioCharts.Core)

Where an annotation label sits along its line or band.

- `Start` — At the start: the left of a horizontal line, the bottom of a vertical line.
- `Middle` — In the middle.
- `End` — At the end: the right of a horizontal line, the top of a vertical line.

#### `ExportFormat` (enum, RioCharts.Blazor)

An export format.

- `Png` — A PNG image.
- `Svg` — An SVG document.
- `Csv` — The chart's data as CSV.

#### `ScaleType` (enum, RioCharts.Core)

The scale of an axis.

- `Auto` — Picked from the data: times give a time axis, numbers a linear axis, strings a band axis.
- `Linear` — A continuous numeric axis.
- `Time` — A continuous time axis with calendar ticks.
- `Band` — Evenly spaced categories.
- `Log` — A logarithmic numeric axis: equal ratios get equal distances, for data that spans several powers of ten. Ticks are powers of ten (with 2 and 5 between them for short ranges). Values of zero or below have no place on it: they are left out (gaps in lines) with a warning. On the x axis for numbers under lines, areas and scatter points, not bars.

#### `AxisPosition` (enum, RioCharts.Core)

Side of a vertical axis.

- `Auto` — The primary axis on the left, additional axes on the right.
- `Left` — On the left of the plot.
- `Right` — On the right of the plot.

#### `StackMode` (enum, RioCharts.Core)

How stacked series add up on their axis.

- `Normal` — Values stack on each other: the top of a stack is the total.
- `Percent` — Each stack fills the axis (100 %): the series show their share of the total per x value.

#### `LegendMode` (enum, RioCharts.Core)

When the legend is shown.

- `Auto` — Only when there is more than one series.
- `Show` — Always.
- `Hide` — Never.

#### `LegendPosition` (enum, RioCharts.Core)

Where the legend sits.

- `Top` — Above the plot.
- `Bottom` — Below the plot.
- `Right` — To the right of the plot (moves to the top when the chart is too narrow).

#### `AnnotationType` (enum, RioCharts.Core)

Kind of annotation.

- `Line` — A reference line at `Annotation.Value` (e.g. a sales target).
- `Band` — A shaded band from `Annotation.From` to `Annotation.To` (e.g. a campaign period).
- `Point` — A marker at `Annotation.X`, `Annotation.Y`.
- `Callout` — A point marker with its label in a text box offset from the point.

#### `SeriesOptions` (record, RioCharts.Core)

One series: its type, where its data comes from (fields and transforms in JSON definitions) and how it looks.

63 properties: `Id`, `Type`, `Dataset`, `X`, `Y`, `Filter`, `TimeBucket`, `Aggregate`, `GroupBy`, `Sort`, `Limit`, `Name`, `Color`, `Curve`, `StrokeWidth`, `ZIndex`, `YAxisId`, `Stack`, `DataLabels`, `Low`, `Open`, `Q1`, `Q3`, `High`, `Row`, `Start`, `End`, `Total`, `BinWidth`, `BinCount`, `MarkerSize`, `MaxBarWidth`, `GroupByCountry`, `Latitude`, `Longitude`, `Size`, `SizeName`, `SizeFormat`, `TrendLine`, `DirectionColors`, `Highlight`, `InnerRadius`, `StartAngle`, `EndAngle`, `GroupSmallSlices`, `Path`, `VisibleLevels`, `ColorBands`, `ColorField`, `PathSeparator`, `Max`, `Min`, `Midpoint`, `BelowColor`, `Target`, `From`, `Error`, `ErrorField`, `ErrorLow`, `ErrorHigh`, `TargetField`, `Format`, `DisplayName`.

#### `DataField` (class, RioCharts.Core.Definitions)

A named column: its type and values (double, DateTime/DateTimeOffset or string; null for missing).

- `Name`: `string` (read-only) — The field name definitions refer to (matched case-insensitively).
- `Type`: `FieldType` (read-only) — The kind of values.
- `Values`: `object?[]` (read-only) — One value per row: double, DateTime/DateTimeOffset or string; null for missing.
- `Description`: `string?` (read-only) — What the field means (shown to AI agents), e.g. "Revenue in €".

- `new DataField(string name, FieldType type, object?[] values, string? description = null)` — Creates a field.

#### `XKind` (enum, RioCharts.Core.Data)

What the x values of a series are.

- `Numeric` — Plain numbers.
- `Time` — Times, stored as milliseconds (see `TimeValue`).
- `Category` — Categories, stored as indexes into `SeriesData.Categories`.

#### `CandleColumns` (class, RioCharts.Core.Data)

The candlestick columns of a `SeriesData`, one entry per point in point order; the point's `SeriesData.Y` is its close. Treat as read-only.

- `Open`: `double[]` (read-only) — The open per point.
- `High`: `double[]` (read-only) — The high per point.
- `Low`: `double[]` (read-only) — The low per point.
- `Count`: `int[]` (read-only) — How many values each candle summarizes (0: not known).

- `CandleSummary At(int point, double close)` — The candle of one point (its close is the series' y value).

#### `BoxColumns` (class, RioCharts.Core.Data)

The box plot columns of a `SeriesData`, one entry per point (in point order; the point's `SeriesData.Y` is its median). Treat as read-only.

- `Min`: `double[]` (read-only) — The lowest value per point, outliers included.
- `Low`: `double[]` (read-only) — The lower whisker end per point.
- `Q1`: `double[]` (read-only) — The lower quartile per point.
- `Q3`: `double[]` (read-only) — The upper quartile per point.
- `High`: `double[]` (read-only) — The upper whisker end per point.
- `Max`: `double[]` (read-only) — The highest value per point, outliers included.
- `Count`: `int[]` (read-only) — How many values each point summarizes (0: not known).
- `OutlierValues`: `double[]` (read-only) — All outliers, grouped by point in point order.
- `OutlierPoints`: `int[]` (read-only) — The point of each outlier in `BoxColumns.OutlierValues`.

- `ReadOnlySpan<double> OutliersOf(int point)` — The outliers of one point.
- `BoxSummary At(int point, double median)` — The summary of one point (its median is the series' y value).

#### `FieldType` (enum, RioCharts.Core.Definitions)

The kind of values in a dataset field.

- `Number` — Numbers (double).
- `Time` — Times (DateTime or DateTimeOffset).
- `Text` — Text (string).
